Hence, $\rho^{p}_{d}/(1-(\log d)/\sqrt{d})\leq\xi^{p}_{d}+\frac{1}{d}$ by part 4 of Fact 3.4 applied to $\xi^{p}_{d}+a=\rho^{p}_{d},\xi^{p}_{d}+a+\Delta=\rho^{p}_{d}/(1-(\log d)/\sqrt{d}).$ Similarly, $\rho^{p}_{d}(1+(\log d)/\sqrt{d})\geq\xi^{p}_{d}-\frac{1}{d}.$ The argument for $\tau^{p}_{d}$ is the same except that one argues about $\langle Z_{1},Z_{2}\rangle/(\|Z_{1}\|_{2}\|Z_{2}\|_{2}=Z_{21}/\|Z_{2}\|_{2}.$ ∎

Combining with the 4-th fact in Fact 3.4, we obtain:

#### Corollary 3.5.

Let $X\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}).$ Suppose that (A) holds $a\in\mathbb{R},\Delta\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ are such that $|a|,|\Delta|\leq(\log d)^{-1}/\sqrt{d}.$ Then, for some absolute constant $C^{\prime\prime}>0,$

$$ {\Delta p}{\sqrt{d}}/(C^{\prime\prime}\sqrt{\log d})\leq\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}\Big[X\in[\tau^{p}_{d}+a,\tau^{p}_{d}+a+\Delta]\Big]\leq{\Delta p}{\sqrt{d}}\times(C^{\prime\prime}\sqrt{\log d}), $$

$$ {\Delta p}{\sqrt{d}}/(C^{\prime\prime}\sqrt{\log d})\leq\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}\Big[X\in[\rho^{p}_{d}+a,\rho^{p}_{d}+a+\Delta]\Big]\leq{\Delta p}{\sqrt{d}}\times(C^{\prime\prime}\sqrt{\log d}), $$

#### Corollary 3.6.

Suppose that (A) holds $a\in\mathbb{R},b\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ are such that $|a|,|\Delta|\leq(\log d)^{-1}/\sqrt{d}.$ Then, for some absolute constant $C^{\prime\prime}>0,$

$$ \displaystyle{\Delta p}{\sqrt{d}}/(C^{\prime\prime}\sqrt{\log d})-e^{-C^{\prime\prime}(\log d)^{2}}\leq\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}_{V_{1},V_{2}\sim_{iid}\mathsf{Unif}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})}\Big[\langle V_{1},V_{2}\rangle\in[\tau^{p}_{d}+a,\tau^{p}_{d}+a+\Delta]\Big]\leq \displaystyle\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\leq{\Delta p}{\sqrt{d}}\times(C^{\prime\prime}\sqrt{\log d})+e^{-C^{\prime\prime}(\log d)^{2}}, \displaystyle{\Delta p}{\sqrt{d}}/(C^{\prime\prime}\sqrt{\log d})-e^{-C^{\prime\prime}(\log d)^{2}}\leq\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}_{Z_{1},Z_{2}\sim_{iid}\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d})}\Big[\langle Z_{1},Z_{2}\rangle\in[\rho^{p}_{d}+a,\rho^{p}_{d}+a+\Delta]\Big]\leq \displaystyle\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\leq{\Delta p}{\sqrt{d}}\times(C^{\prime\prime}\sqrt{\log d})+e^{-C^{\prime\prime}(\log d)^{2}}. $$

#### Proof.

The proofs in the Gaussian and spherical settings are essentially the same. In the Gaussian case, we write $\langle Z_{1},Z_{2}\rangle=Z_{11}Z_{21}.$ Then, we condition on $Z_{11}\in 1\pm(\log d)/\sqrt{d}$ as in Proposition 3.6 which happens with probability $1-\exp(-\Omega((\log d)^{2})).$ Then, we are in the setting of Corollary 3.5 with a value of $\Delta$ changed by a multiplicative factor of $1\pm O(\log d/\sqrt{d}).$ We apply Corollary 3.5. ∎

## 4 Distinguishing Spherical RGG and Erdős-Rényi

#### Proof of Theorem 1.5.

Suppose that $d\geq(M^{1/2}p)^{3+c}$ for some constant $c>0.$ Let $D=(\log n)^{1.1}$ and $\mathbf{G}_{0}\sim\mathsf{G}(N,p),\mathbf{G}_{1}\sim\mathsf{RGG}(N,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},p).$ In light of Claim 3.1, we simply need to show that

$$ \sum_{H\subseteq E(\mathcal{M})\;:\;1\leq|E(H)|\leq D}\Big(\Phi^{p}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},p)}(H)\Big)^{2}=o_{n}(1). $$

Note that each isomorphic copy of $H$ has the same Fourier coefficient under the ${\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},p)}$ distribution. Hence, if $N(H,\mathcal{M})$ denotes the number of subgraphs of $\mathcal{M},$ this is equivalent to

$$ \sum_{H\in\mathcal{G}_{D}}N(H,\mathcal{M})\Big(\Phi^{p}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},p)}(H)\Big)^{2}=o_{n}(1). $$

A beautiful result in [Alo81] shows that $N(H,\mathcal{M})\leq C^{|V(H)|^{1.1}}M^{(|V(H)|+\delta(H))/2}$ for all $H$ and $M$ -vertex graphs $\mathcal{M},$ where $C$ is some absolute constant.33 3 [Alo81] explicitly only shows that $N(H,\mathcal{M})\leq C_{H}M^{(|V(H)|+\delta(H))/2}$ where $C_{H}$ is some constant depending only on $H.$ However, one can easily track in the argument this constant to be $|V(H)|^{O(|V(H)|)}$ which is enough. In fact, Alon shows that this result is tight up to the choice of constant $C_{H}.$

By Proposition 3.2, it is enough to consider the case when $H$ has no leaves.

Now, we will use Theorems 1.1 and 1.2. Observe that for $H$ connected, $\mathsf{OEI}(H)\geq\frac{1}{3}(2\lceil\frac{|V(H)|-1}{2}\rceil+\delta(H)+1)\geq\frac{|V(H)|+\delta(H)}{3}.$ However, as all of $\mathsf{OEI}(H),|V(H)|,\delta(H)$ are obviously additive over disjoint unions, the inequality $\mathsf{OEI}(H)\geq\frac{|V(H)|+\delta(H)}{3}$ holds for disconnected $H$ as well. We obtain:

$$ \begin{split}&\sum_{H\in\mathcal{NLG}_{D}}N(H,\mathcal{M})\Big(\Phi^{p}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},p)}(H)\Big)^{2}\\
&\leq\sum_{H\in\mathcal{NLG}_{D}}C^{|V(H)|^{1.1}}M^{(|V(H)|+\delta(H))/2}\times\Big(\Big(8\sqrt{\frac{p}{1-p}})^{|E(H)|}\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{4}}{\sqrt{d}}\Big)^{\mathsf{OEI}(H)}\Big)^{2}\\
&\leq\sum_{H\in\mathcal{NLG}_{D}}C^{|V(H)|^{1.1}}128^{|E(H)|}p^{|E(H)|}M^{(|V(H)|+\delta(H))/2}\times\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{8}}{d}\Big)^{(|V(H)|+\delta(H))/3}.\end{split} $$

Now, we use the following proposition.

#### Proposition 4.1.

Suppose that $H$ is a graph without isolated vertices and leaves. Then, $|E(H)|\geq|V(H)|+\delta(H).$

#### Proof.

Note that in a graph $H$ without isolated vertices and leaves, each vertex has degree at least $2.$ By Proposition 2.1, there exists some independent set $S$ such that $|S|-|N_{H}(S)|=\delta(H)$ and, hence, $S\cap N_{H}(S)=\emptyset.$ In particular, this means that among the vertices $A=S\cup N_{H}(S),$ there are at least $2|S|$ edges with both endpoints in $A$ (as each vertex in $S$ has at least two neighbours and both are in $N_{H}(S)$ by definition of $N_{H}(\cdot)$ ). On the other hand, each vertex in $V(H)\backslash A$ is also adjacent to at least two edges, so there are at least $\frac{1}{2}\times 2(|V(H)|-|A|)$ more edges. Altogether, this means that the number of edges in $H$ is at least

$$ 2|S|+(|V(H)|-|A|)=2|S|+|V(H)|-|S|-|N_{H}(S)|=|V(H)|+|S|-|N_{H}(S)|=|V(H)|+\delta(H), $$

as desired. ∎

Going back to Eq. 22, we bound

$$ \begin{split}&\sum_{H\in\mathcal{NLG}_{D}}C^{|V(H)|^{1.1}}128^{|E(H)|}p^{|E(H)|}M^{(|V(H)|+\delta(H))/2}\times\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{8}}{d}\Big)^{(|V(H)|+\delta(H))/3}\\
&\leq\sum_{H\in\mathcal{NLG}_{D}}C^{|V(H)|^{1.1}}128^{|E(H)|}p^{|V(H)|+\delta(H)}M^{(|V(H)|+\delta(H))/2}\times\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{8}}{d}\Big)^{(|V(H)|+\delta(H))/3}\\
&=\sum_{H\in\mathcal{NLG}_{D}}C^{|V(H)|^{1.1}}128^{|E(H)|}\Big(\frac{M^{1/2}p(\log n)^{8}}{d^{1/3}}\Big)^{(|V(H)|+\delta(H))}\\
\end{split} $$

As $d\geq(M^{1/2}p)^{3+c},$ under (A), $\Big(\frac{M^{1/2}p(\log n)^{8}}{d^{1/3}}\Big)\leq n^{-\theta}$ for some constant $\theta>0$ (depending only on $\delta,\gamma$ from (A), and $c$ from Theorem 1.5). Recall that $M=\Theta(n^{2}).$ Also, $\delta(H)\geq 0$ (by taking $S=V(H)$ in the definition). Hence, we can bound Eq. 23 by

$$ \begin{split}&\sum_{H\in\mathcal{NLG}_{D}}C^{|V(H)|^{1.1}}128^{|E(H)|}\Big(\frac{M^{1/2}p(\log n)^{8}}{d^{1/3}}\Big)^{(|V(H)|+\delta(H))}\\
&\leq\sum_{H\in\mathcal{NLG}_{D}}C^{|V(H)|^{1.1}}128^{|E(H)|}n^{-|V(H)|\theta}=\sum_{H\in\mathcal{NLG}_{D}}C^{|V(H)|^{1.1}}128^{|E(H)|}e^{-|V(H)|\theta\log n}.\end{split} $$

Note that $|V(H)|\leq 2|E(H)|\leq 2D=O((\log n)^{1.1}).$ Thus, $|V(H)|^{1.1}=o_{n}(|V(H)|\log n).$ Similarly, $E(H)\leq\min(|V(H)|^{2},D)\leq|V(H)|D^{1/2}=o_{n}(|V(H)|\log n).$ Hence, for all large enough $n,$ the expression above is bounded by

$$ \sum_{H\in\mathcal{NLG}_{D}}e^{-\frac{\theta}{2}|V(H)|\log n}. $$

The last expression is bounded by $\sum_{H\in\mathcal{G}_{D}}e^{-\frac{\theta}{2}|V(H)|\log n}$ which is enough by Proposition 3.1. ∎

## 5 Distinguishing Gaussian RGG and Erdős-Rényi

### 5.1 Proof of Theorem 1.6

#### 5.1.1 Detection Lower Bound

Suppose that $d\geq\max(n^{3/2}p)^{1+c},(n^{3}p^{3})^{1+c}).$ We will prove that no degree $D=(\log n)^{1.1}$ polynomial distinguishes the two graph models. We proceed as in Section 4 with $\mathcal{M}=K_{n}.$ Using the obvious bound $N(K_{n},H)\leq n^{|V(H)|}$ (as one can choose each of the $|V(H)|$ labeled vertices of $H$ in at most $n$ ways), we need to show the following analogue of Eq. 21.

$$ \sum_{H\in\mathcal{G}_{D}}n^{|V(H)|}\Big(\Phi^{p}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}(H)\Big)^{2}=o_{n}(1). $$

Now, consider any graph $H$ on $v$ vertices and $e$ edges. Suppose that its connected components are $H_{1},H_{2},\ldots,H_{r},$ where $H_{i}$ has $v_{i}$ vertices and $e_{i}$ edges. Clearly, $\sum_{i=1}^{r}e_{i}=e,\sum_{i=1}^{r}v_{i}=v$ and $\Phi^{p}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}(H)=\prod_{i=1}^{r}\Phi^{p}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}(H_{i}).$ Clearly, if any of the graphs $H_{i}$ is a single edge, $\Phi^{p}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}(H_{i})=0,$ so we can focus on the case $e_{i}\geq 2,v_{i}\geq 3$ $\forall i.$ Now, suppose that $H_{1},H_{2},\ldots,H_{t}$ are trees and $H_{t+1},H_{t+2},\ldots,H_{r}$ are not. Then, using Proposition 3.3,

- 1. For $1\leq u\leq r,$ $\displaystyle\Big|\Phi^{p}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}(H_{i})\Big|=\Big|\Big(\sqrt{\frac{1}{p(1-p)}}\Big)^{e_{i}}\E[\prod_{(uv)\in E(H_{i})}(G_{uv}-p)]\Big|$ $\displaystyle\leq\Big(\sqrt{\frac{1}{p(1-p)}}\Big)^{e_{i}}\Big(\frac{p(\log n)^{4}}{\sqrt{d}}\Big)^{e_{i}}\leq\Big(\frac{2p(\log n)^{8}}{d}\Big)^{v_{i}/3}.$ We used $e_{i}=v_{i}-1\geq 2v_{i}/3$ twice.

- 2. For $r+1\leq u\leq t,$ $\displaystyle\Big|\Phi^{p}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}(H_{i})\Big|=\Big|\Big(\sqrt{\frac{1}{p(1-p)}}\Big)^{e_{i}}\E[\prod_{(uv)\in E(H_{i})}(G_{uv}-p)]\Big|$ $\displaystyle\leq\Big(\sqrt{\frac{1}{p(1-p)}}\Big)^{e_{i}}p^{e_{i}}\times\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{4}}{\sqrt{d}}\Big)^{\lceil(v_{i}-1)/2\rceil}\leq(2\sqrt{p})^{e_{i}}\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{4}}{\sqrt{d}}\Big)^{v_{i}/3}\leq\Big(\frac{8p^{3}(\log n)^{4}}{\sqrt{d}}\Big)^{v_{i}/3}.$ This time, we used $v_{i}\geq e_{i}$ (as $H_{i}$ is connected and not a tree) and $\lceil(v_{i}-1)/2\rceil\geq v_{i}/3.$

Altogether, this means that

$$ \Big|\Phi^{p}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}(H)\Big|\leq\Big(\frac{2p(\log n)^{8}}{d}\Big)^{\sum_{i=1}^{r}v_{i}/3}\times\Big(\frac{8p^{3/2}(\log n)^{4}}{\sqrt{d}}\Big)^{\sum_{i=r+1}^{t}v_{i}/3}. $$

Hence, as $|V(H)|=\sum_{i=1}^{t}v_{i},$

$$ n^{|V(H)|}\Phi^{p}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}(H)^{2}\leq\Big(\frac{2p(\log n)^{8}n^{3/2}}{d}\Big)^{\sum_{i=1}^{r}2v_{i}/3}\times\Big(\frac{8p^{3}n^{3}(\log n)^{4}}{{d}}\Big)^{\sum_{i=r+1}^{t}v_{i}/3}. $$

As $d\geq(n^{3/2}p)^{1+c},d\geq(n^{3}p^{3})^{1+c}$ and (A) holds, this last expression is clearly at most $n^{-\theta|V(H)|}$ for some absolute constant $\theta$ depending only on $\epsilon,\gamma$ from (A) and $c$ from Theorem 1.7. The claim follows from Proposition 3.1.

#### 5.1.2 Detection Algorithms

#### 1. Detecting via signed wedges.

We want to show that if $d=o\Big((n^{3/2}p)(\log n)^{-4}\Big),p\leq 0.49$ and (A) holds, the signed wedge count statistic distinguishes ${\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}$ and $\mathsf{G}(n,p)$ with high probability in the sense of Definition 8. The condition $p<0.49$ is needed as ${\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}$ and ${\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),\frac{1}{2})}$ are the same distribution.

Recall the definition of signed counts Eq. 17. By Lemma 3.2,

$$ \E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}}[\mathsf{CS}^{p}_{\wedge}(\mathbf{G})]=n\binom{n-1}{2}\E[\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{\wedge(1,2,3)}(\mathbf{G})]\geq\frac{n^{3}p^{2}}{4d}\times(\log d)^{-4}. $$

Clearly, $\E_{\mathbf{H}\sim\mathsf{\mathbf{G}}(n,p)}[\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{\wedge}(\mathbf{H})]=0.$ Now, we compute the variances. Note that, with respect to either distribution,

$$ \mathsf{Var}\Big[\mathsf{CS}^{p}_{\wedge}\Big]=\sum_{(i,j,k)}\mathsf{Var}[\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{\wedge(i,j,k)}]+\sum_{\wedge(i,j,k)\neq\wedge(i^{\prime},j^{\prime},k^{\prime})}\mathsf{Cov}[\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{\wedge(i,j,k)},\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{\wedge(i^{\prime},j^{\prime},k^{\prime})}]. $$

Importantly, observe that for any two labelled subgraphs $H_{1},H_{2},$ one has $\mathsf{Cov}[\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{H_{1}},\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{H_{2}}]=\E[\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{H_{1}}\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{H_{2}}]-\E[\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{H_{1}}]\E[\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{H_{2}}].$ However,

$$ \begin{split}&\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{H_{1}}(G)\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{H_{2}}(G)\\
&=\prod_{e_{1}\in E(H_{1})}(G_{e_{1}}-p)\times\prod_{e_{2}\in E(H_{2})}(G_{e_{2}}-p)\\
&=\prod_{e\in E(H_{1})\triangle E(H_{2})}(G_{e}-p)\times\prod_{e\in E(H_{1})\cap E(H_{2})}(G_{e}-p)^{2}\\
&=\prod_{e\in E(H_{1})\triangle E(H_{2})}(G_{e}-p)\times\prod_{e\in E(H_{1})\cap E(H_{2})}((G_{e}-p)(1-2p)+(p-p^{2}))\\
&=\sum_{A\subseteq E(H_{1})\cap E(H_{2})}\prod_{e\in(E(H_{1})\triangle E(H_{2}))\cup A}(G_{e}-p)(1-2p)^{|A|}(p-p^{2})^{|E(H_{1})\cap E(H_{2})|-|A|}.\end{split} $$

In particular, the covariance is also easily expressed as a linear combination of signed weights (which should be no surprise as any polynomial can be expanded in the Fourier basis). The above expression immediately shows that unless $H_{1}=H_{2},$ the covariance with respect to $\mathsf{G}(n,p)$ is 0 as an edge in $E(H_{1})\triangle E(H_{2})$ has expectation $0.$ When $H_{1}=H_{2}=\wedge(i,j,k),$ the covariance is bounded by $p^{|E(H)|}=p^{2}.$ Hence, $\mathsf{Var}_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{G}(n,p)}\Big[\mathsf{CS}^{p}_{\wedge}(\mathbf{G})\Big]=O(n^{3}p^{2})$ For the geometric distribution, we can use Proposition 3.3 to bound the covariance. We carry out this trivial calculation in Section A.1 and show that $\mathsf{Var}_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{RGG}}\Big[\mathsf{CS}^{p}_{\wedge}(\mathbf{G})\Big]=o\Big((\log d)^{8}\times\Big(n^{3}p^{2}+n^{5}p^{4}/d^{2}+n^{4}p^{3}/d+n^{4}p^{4}/d^{2}\Big)\Big),$ which is enough to conclude by Definition 8.

#### 2. Detecting via signed triangles.

We want to show that if $d=o\Big((n^{3}p^{3})(\log n)^{-1}\Big)$ for some absolute constant $c$ and (A) holds, the signed triangle count statistic distinguishes ${\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}$ and $\mathsf{G}(n,p).$ The proof is analogous to the ones given in [BDER14, LMSY22], but we give it for completeness. We will use the following claim, the proof of which is presented in Section A.5.

#### Lemma 5.1.

$\displaystyle\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}}\Big[\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{\triangle}(\mathbf{G})\Big]\geq\frac{Cp^{3}(\log d)^{-1}}{\sqrt{d}}$ for some absolute constant $C.$

As in the proof for wedges, we know that $\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}}[\mathsf{CS}^{p}_{\triangle}(\mathbf{G})]\geq\frac{Cn^{3}p^{3}(\log d)^{-1}}{6\sqrt{d}},$ $\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{G}(n,p)}[\mathsf{CS}^{p}_{\triangle}(\mathbf{G})]=0,\mathsf{Var}_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{G}(n,p)}[\mathsf{CS}^{p}_{\triangle}(\mathbf{G})]=\Theta(n^{3}p^{3}).$ In Section A.2 we show that $\mathsf{Var}_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{RGG}}[\mathsf{CS}^{p}_{\triangle}(\mathbf{G})]=O\Big(n^{5}p^{6}(\log d)^{4}/d+n^{4}p^{5}(\log d)^{4}/d+n^{3}p^{3}\Big),$ which is enough.

### 5.2 Proof of Theorem 1.7

#### 5.2.1 Detection Lower Bounds

Suppose that $d\geq\max\Big((Mp)^{1+c},(M^{3/2}p^{3})^{1+c}\Big).$ We want to show that for all $\mathcal{M}$ on $M$ edges and $N$ vertices, the distributions $\mathbf{G}_{0}\sim\mathsf{G}(N,p)\odot\mathcal{M},\mathbf{G}_{1}\sim\mathsf{RGG}(N,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)$ are indistinguishable with respect to low degree polynomials. As in Section 4, we simply need to show that

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{H\in\mathcal{G}_{D}}C^{|V(H)|^{1.1}}\times M^{(|V(H)|+\delta(H))/2}\times\Big(\Phi^{p}_{{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}}(H)\Big)^{2}=o_{n}(1). $$

Decompose $H$ into $\mathsf{TP}(H)$ and $\mathsf{NLP}(H)$ as in Definition 10. Let $\mathsf{TP}(H)$ be composed of trees $T_{1},T_{2},\ldots,T_{k}.$ We will use the following claim.

#### Proposition 5.1.

Let $H$ be a graph. Suppose that there exist two graphs $H_{1},H_{2}$ such that $|V(H_{1})\cap V(H_{2})|\leq 1$ and $E(H)=E(H_{1})\cup E(H_{2}).$ Then,

$$ |V(H)|+\delta(H)\leq(|V(H_{1})|+\delta(H_{1}))+(|V(H_{2})|+\delta(H_{2})). $$

#### Proof.

If $|V(H_{1})\cap V(H_{2})|=0,$ this claim is trivial as both $|V(H)|$ and $\delta(H)$ are additive over disjoint unions. Suppose that $V(H_{1})\cap V(H_{2})=\{a\}.$ Let $S\in\arg\max_{S^{\prime}\subseteq V(H)}|S^{\prime}|-|N_{H}(S^{\prime})|.$ Let $S_{1}=S\cap V(H_{1}),S_{2}=S\cap V(H_{2}).$ It is enough to show that

$$ \displaystyle|V(H)|+|S|-|N_{H}(S)|\leq|V(H_{1})|+|S_{1}|-|N_{H_{1}}(S_{1})|+|V(H_{2})|+|S_{2}|-|N_{H_{2}}(S_{2})|\;\Longleftrightarrow \displaystyle|S|+|N_{H_{1}}(S_{1})|+|N_{H_{2}}(S_{2})|\leq|S_{1}|+|S_{2}|+|N_{H}(S_{1}\cup S_{2})|+1. $$

Now, observe that $|S|\leq|S_{1}|+|S_{2}|$ trivially. However, $|N_{H_{1}}(S_{1})|+|N_{H_{2}}(S_{2})|\leq|N_{H}(S_{1}\cup S_{2})|+1.$ Indeed, this holds as $N_{H_{1}}(S_{1})\cup N_{H_{2}}(S_{2})\subseteq N_{H}(S_{1}\cup S_{2})$ and $N_{H_{1}}(S_{1})\cap N_{H_{2}}(S_{2})\subseteq\{a\}.$ ∎

As each tree $T_{i}$ has at most one common vertex with $\mathsf{NLP}(H)$ and none with other trees, we apply the above lemma inductively and obtain

$$ |V(H)|+\delta(H)\leq\sum_{i=1}^{k}(|V(T_{i})|+\delta(T_{i}))+|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H))|+\delta(\mathsf{NLP}(H)). $$

Using Proposition 3.3, we bound Eq. 26 as follows.

$$ \begin{split}&\sum_{H\in\mathcal{G}_{D}}C^{|V(H)|^{1.1}}\times M^{(|V(H)|+\delta(H))/2}\times p^{|E(H)|}\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{10}}{\sqrt{d}}\Big)^{2|E(\mathsf{TP}(H))|+2\mathsf{OEI}(\mathsf{NLP}(H))}\\
&\leq\sum_{H\in\mathcal{G}_{D}}C^{|V(H)|^{1.1}}\times M^{\sum_{i=1}^{k}(|V(T_{i})|+\delta(T_{i}))/2+(|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H))|+\delta(\mathsf{NLP}(H)))/2}\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\times p^{\sum_{i=1}^{t}|E(T_{i})|+|E(\mathsf{NLP}(H))|}\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{10}}{\sqrt{d}}\Big)^{2\sum_{i=1}^{t}|E(T_{i})|+2\mathsf{OEI}(\mathsf{NLP}(H))}.\end{split} $$

Now, we use the following simple combinatorial claim.

#### Claim 5.2.

For any non-empty tree $T,$ $\delta(T)\leq|V(T)|-2.$

#### Proof.

Suppose, for the sake of contradiction, that $\delta(T)\geq|V(T)|-1.$ As in Proposition 2.1, there exists some independent set $S$ such that $\delta(T)=|S|-|N_{T}(S)|.$ Hence, $|S|\geq|V(T)|-1.$ As $T$ is connected, $|N_{T}(S)|\geq 1.$ As $S$ is independent, $S\subseteq V(T)\backslash N_{T}(S),$ so $|S|\leq|V(T)|-1.$ Altogether, $\delta(T)=|S|-|N_{T}(S)|\leq|V(T)|-2,$ contradiction. ∎

We also use $V(\mathsf{NLP}(H))+\delta(\mathsf{NLP}(H))\leq|E(H)|$ from Proposition 4.1 as $\mathsf{NLP}(H)$ has minimal degree $2$ and $\mathsf{OEI}(H)\geq\frac{|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H))|+\delta(H)}{3}$ from Proposition 1.2.

Combining these, we bound the last expression by

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{H\in\mathcal{G}_{D}}C^{|V(H)|^{1.1}}\times M^{\sum_{i=1}^{k}(|V(T_{i})|-1)+(|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H))|+\delta(\mathsf{NLP}(H)))/2}\times \displaystyle\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad p^{\sum_{i=1}^{t}|E(T_{i})|+|E(H)|}\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{10}}{\sqrt{d}}\Big)^{2\sum_{i=1}^{t}|E(T_{i})|+2\frac{|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H))|+\delta(H)}{3}} \displaystyle\leq\sum_{H\in\mathcal{G}_{D}}C^{|V(H)|^{1.1}}\times M^{\sum_{i=1}^{k}|E(T_{i})|+(|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H))|+\delta(\mathsf{NLP}(H)))/2}\times \displaystyle\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad p^{\sum_{i=1}^{t}|E(T_{i})|+(|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H))|+\delta(\mathsf{NLP}(H)))}\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{10}}{\sqrt{d}}\Big)^{2\sum_{i=1}^{t}|E(T_{i})|+2\frac{|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H))|+\delta(H)}{3}} \displaystyle\leq\sum_{H\in\mathcal{G}_{D}}C^{|V(H)|^{1.1}}\times\prod_{i=1}^{t}\Big(\frac{Mp(\log n)^{20}}{d}\Big)^{|E(T_{i})|}\times\Big(\frac{M^{3/2}p^{3}(\log n)^{20}}{d}\Big)^{(|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H))|+\delta(H))/3}. $$

Now, whenever $d\geq\max\Big((Mp)^{1+c},(M^{3/2}p^{3})^{1+c}\Big),$ this last expression is bounded by $n^{-\theta|V(H)|}$ for some absolute constant $\theta$ under $\eqref{eq:assumption}.$ As $|V(H)|=O(D)=O((\log n)^{1.1}),$ the entire expression is bounded by

$$ \sum_{H\in\mathcal{G}_{D}}C^{|V(H)|^{1.1}}n^{-\theta|V(H)|}\leq\sum_{H\in\mathcal{G}_{D}}n^{-\theta|V(H)|/2}=o_{n}(1), $$

the last following from Proposition 3.1.

#### 5.2.2 Detection Algorithm

To detect with sample complexity $M=d(\log d)^{17}/p,$ choose a mask $\mathcal{M}$ which is the union of $A=(\log n)^{17}$ disjoint stars on $N=d$ leaves. Then, $M=AN=(Np)(\log d)^{17}$ Observe that all subgraphs are stars and the number of $\mathsf{Star}_{k}$ subgraphs is $A\times\binom{N}{k}=\Theta(AN^{k})$ for $k$ constant.

By Lemma 3.2, the expect signed count of wedges is

$$ \E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}}[\mathsf{CS}_{\wedge}]=\Theta\Big(AN^{2}\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}}[\mathsf{SW}_{\wedge(1,2,3)(\mathbf{G})}]\Big)=\Omega(AN^{2}p^{2}(\log d)^{-4}/d). $$

The expectation with respect to $\mathsf{G}(n,p)$ is clearly 0 and the variance $\Theta(AN^{2}p^{2}).$ As in the unmasked case, we analyze the variance with respect to ${\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}$ in Section A.3 based on the overlap patterns and show that it is of order $O\Big(AN^{4}p^{4}(\log d)^{8}/d^{2}+AN^{3}p^{3}(\log n)^{4}/d+AN^{2}p^{2}\Big)$ which is enough for the condition in Definition 8 to hold.

## 6 RGG versus Planted Coloring

Our first step is to choose $q$ appropriately. We do this in such a way that the “most informative” triangle Fourier coefficients of $\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},1/2)$ and $\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)$ (nearly) match.

After that, we follow nearly explicitly the method of [KVWX23] for proving low-degree indistinguishability to $\mathsf{PCol}(n,q).$ It is based on a clever analysis of the bound in Definition 9 exploiting the ambient Erdős-Rényi structure of $\mathsf{PCol}(n,q).$ As a large part of the analysis is nearly identical to [KVWX23], we delay many of the proofs to Appendix B.

### 6.1 Choice of $q$

From Theorem 1.1 and [BDER14, Lemma 1], it immediately follows that $\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},1/2)}[\mathsf{SW}_{\triangle}(\mathbf{G})]\in\Big[\frac{(\log d)^{-1}}{\sqrt{d}},\frac{\log d}{\sqrt{d}}\Big].$ We want to find some $q$ which leads to the same signed expectation of a triangle in $\mathsf{PCol}(n,q).$ Computing signed expectations for $\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)$ is very easy with the same strategy for computing Fourier coefficients as in the planted clique case described in Section 1.2.

#### Proposition 6.1.

Consider some graph $H$ and $\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{PCol}(n,q).$ Then,

- 1. If $H$ has a leaf, $\E[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H}(\mathbf{G})]=0.$

- 2. $\E[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{\triangle}(\mathbf{G})]=\frac{1}{8q^{2}}+\frac{3}{8(q-1)q^{2}}-\frac{(q-2)}{8q^{2}(q-1)^{2}}$

- 3. $|\E[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H}]|\leq\Big(\frac{|V(H)|}{q}\Big)^{|V(H)|-|\mathsf{CC}(H)|}.$

We prove this proposition in Section B.1 and now continue to the choice of $q.$ We define $q$ by rounding some real $q_{1}$ which exactly matches the signed triangle expectation.

$$ \begin{split}&\frac{1}{8q_{1}^{2}}+\frac{3}{8(q_{1}-1)q_{1}^{2}}-\frac{(q_{1}-2)}{8_{1}q^{2}(q_{1}-1)^{2}}\coloneqq\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},1/2)}[\mathsf{SW}_{\triangle}(\mathbf{G})]\in\Big[\frac{(\log d)^{-1}}{\sqrt{d}},\frac{\log d}{\sqrt{d}}\Big].\\
&q\coloneqq\lceil q_{1}\rceil.\end{split} $$

With this, one immediately concludes that

$$ \begin{split}&q\in\Big[{d^{1/4}}/(\log d),{d^{1/4}}(\log d)\Big],\\
&\Big|\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{\triangle}(\mathbf{G})]-\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},p)}}[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{\triangle}(\mathbf{G})]\Big|\leq\frac{1}{q^{3}}\leq\frac{(\log d)^{3}}{d^{3/4}}.\end{split} $$

Similarly, for any connected graph $H$ on at most $D=(\log n)^{1.1}$ edges and at least 4 vertices, one can observe that

$$ \begin{split}&\Big|\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H}(\mathbf{G})]-\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},p)}}[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H}(\mathbf{G})]\Big|\\
&\leq\Big|\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H}(\mathbf{G})]\Big|+\Big|\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},p)}}[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H}(\mathbf{G})]\Big|\\
&\leq\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{4}}{\sqrt{d}}\Big)^{\lceil(|V(H)|-1)/2\rceil}+\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{2}}{q}\Big)^{(|V(H)|-1)}\leq\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{8}}{q}\Big)^{(|V(H)|-1)}.\end{split} $$

Combining with Eq. 28 and using the fact that when $H$ has a leaf, both signed weights equal 0, we reach the following conclusion.

#### Proposition 6.2.

For any graph $H$ on at most $D=(\log n)^{1.1}$ vertices,

$$ \Big|\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H}(\mathbf{G})]-\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},p)}}[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H}(\mathbf{G})]\Big|\leq D\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{8}}{q}\Big)^{\max(3,|V(H)|-|\mathsf{CC}(H)|)}. $$

#### Proof.

If $H$ is connected, this follows immediately from Eqs. 28 and 6.1. Otherwise, assume that $H$ has $i$ connected components $H_{1},H_{2},\ldots,H_{i},$ where necessarily $i\leq D.$ If one of them is on less than 3 vertices, $H$ has a leaf and, hence, the entire expression is equal to zero. Thus, we assume that each $H_{i}$ is on at least 3 vertices. Now, we use triangle inequality and multiplicativity of $\mathsf{SW}_{H}$ under disjoint connected components as follows.

$$ \displaystyle\Big|\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H}(\mathbf{G})]-\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},p)}}[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H}(\mathbf{G})]\Big| \displaystyle\leq\prod_{H_{i}\in\mathsf{CC}(H)}\Big(\Big|\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H_{i}}(\mathbf{G})]-\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},p)}}[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H_{i}}(\mathbf{G})]\Big|\times \displaystyle\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\times\Big|\prod_{j=1}^{i-1}\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H_{j}}(\mathbf{G})]\prod_{j=i+1}^{|\mathsf{CC}(H)|}\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},p)}}[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H_{j}}(\mathbf{G})]\Big|\Big). $$

The conclusion follows. ∎

### 6.2 Low-Degree Indistinguishability With Respect To Planted Coloring

Denote $\psi_{q}\coloneqq 1/2-1/(2(q-1)).$ Observe that the planted coloring model can be generated in the following way. One first samples $\mathbf{H}\sim\mathsf{G}(n,\psi_{q}).$ Then, one samples $\mathbf{X}$ by assigning a uniform label over $[q]$ to each vertex and drawing an edge between $i,j$ if and only if $i$ and $j$ have the same label. Denote by $\mathsf{L}(n,q)$ the distribution of $\mathbf{X}.$ Then, the union of $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{H}$ given by $\mathbf{X}\vee\mathbf{H}$ is distributed as $\mathsf{PCol}(n,q).$ This representation explicitly captures the ambient Erdős-Rényi structure. Using it, the authors of [KVWX23] derive an analogue of Claim 3.1 for low-degree indistinguishability against a planted coloring model. In their case, the planted coloring has density $1/2$ rather than $\psi_{q}$ between vertices with distinct labels. Hence, we state and prove in Section B.3 the variant for $\psi_{q}$ explicitly, even though the arguments are straightforward modifications of those in [KVWX23].

#### Proposition 6.3 (Low-Degree Indistinguishability from $\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)$ ).

Consider ${\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},p)}$ and the $\psi_{q}=(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2(q-1)})$ -based Fourier coefficients given by

$$ \Phi^{\psi_{q}}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}(H)\coloneqq\sqrt{\psi_{q}(1-\psi_{q})}^{-|E(H)|}\times\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}}[\mathsf{SW}^{\psi_{q}}_{H}(\mathbf{G})]. $$

For $K,H$ such that $E(K)\subseteq E(H)\subseteq E(K_{n})$ and $0\leq|E(H)|\leq D,$ define

$$ M_{K,H}\coloneqq\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[\mathbf{X}|_{E(H)}=E(H)\backslash E(K)]\sqrt{(1-\psi_{q})/\psi_{q}}^{E(H)\backslash E(K)}, $$

where $\mathbf{X}|_{E(H)}$ denotes the induced subgraph of $\mathbf{X}$ indexed by edges $E(H).$ Also, recursively define $w_{H}$ for $E(H)\subseteq E(K_{n})$ and $0\leq|E(H)|\leq D,$ where $w_{\emptyset}=1$ and

$$ \displaystyle w_{H}=\frac{1}{M_{H,H}}\Big(\Phi^{\psi_{q}}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}(H)-\sum_{K\subsetneq H}w_{K}M_{K,H}\Big). $$

We define $w_{H}$ to equal $+\infty$ if division by zero occurs in $1/M_{H,H}.$ Then,

$$ \sup_{f\;:\;\mathsf{deg}(f)\leq D}\frac{\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},p)}}[f(\mathbf{G})]}{\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}[f(\mathbf{G})^{2}]}-1\leq\sum_{H\subseteq E(K_{n})\;:\;1\leq|E(H)|\leq D}w_{H}^{2}. $$

Thus, all we need to do is show that $\sum_{H\subseteq E(K_{n})\;:\;1\leq|E(H)|\leq D}w_{H}^{2}=o_{n}(1).$

### 6.3 Bounds on The Weights $w_{H}$

As in [KVWX23], we will instead work with the quantities $\widehat{w}_{H}$ defined by $\widehat{w}_{H}\coloneqq M_{H,H}w_{H}.$ First, one can observe that the recurrence Eq. 29 turns into

$$ \widehat{w}_{H}=\Phi^{\psi_{q}}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}(H)-\sum_{K\subsetneq H}w_{K}M_{K,H}=\Phi^{\psi_{q}}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}(H)-M_{\emptyset,H}-\sum_{\emptyset\subsetneq K\subsetneq H}\widehat{w}_{K}\frac{M_{K,H}}{M_{H,H}}. $$

Note, however, that

$$ \begin{split}&M_{\emptyset,H}=\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[\mathbf{X}|_{E(H)}=E(H)]\sqrt{(1-\psi_{q})/\psi_{q}}^{E(H)}\\
&=(\psi_{q})^{|E(H)|}\sqrt{(1-\psi_{q})/\psi_{q}}^{E(H)}=\sqrt{(1-\psi_{q})/\psi_{q}}^{-E(H)}(1-\psi_{q})^{E(H)}\\
&=\sqrt{(1-\psi_{q})\psi_{q}}^{-E(H)}\sum_{K\subseteq H}\Big(\E_{\mathbf{H}\sim\mathsf{G}(n,\psi_{q}),\mathbf{X}\sim\mathsf{L}(n,q)}\Big[\prod_{(ji)\in E(H)}((\mathbf{X}\vee\mathbf{H})_{(ji)}-\psi_{q})\Big|\mathbf{X}|_{E(H)}=E(H)\backslash E(K)\Big]\times\\
&\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[\mathbf{X}|_{E(H)}=E(H)\backslash E(K)\Big]\Big)\\
&=\sqrt{(1-\psi_{q})\psi_{q}}^{-E(H)}\E\Big[\prod_{(ji)\in E(H)}((\mathbf{X}\vee\mathbf{H})_{(ji)}-\psi_{q})\Big]=\Phi^{\psi_{q}}_{\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}(H).\end{split} $$

Indeed, this holds as $\E_{\mathbf{H}\sim\mathsf{G}(n,\psi_{q}),\mathbf{X}\sim\mathsf{L}(n,q)}[\prod_{(ji)\in E(H)}((\mathbf{X}\vee\mathbf{H})_{(ji)}-\psi_{q})|\mathbf{X}|_{E(H)}=E(H)\backslash E(K)]$ vanishes if $E(K)\neq E(H)$ and whenever $E(H)=E(K),$ equals $(1-\psi_{q})^{|E(H)|}.$ Hence,

$$ \widehat{w}_{H}=(\Phi^{\psi_{q}}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}(H)-\Phi^{\psi_{q}}_{\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}(H))-\sum_{\emptyset\subsetneq K\subsetneq H}\widehat{w}_{K}\frac{M_{K,H}}{M_{K,K}}. $$

Next, we bound the values of $M_{H,H}.$

#### Proposition 6.4.

$M_{H,H}\geq 1-\frac{|V(H)|^{2}}{q}.$

#### Proof.

Observe that $M_{H,H}=\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[\mathbf{X}|_{E(H)}=\emptyset].$ by definition. This happens, in particular, if all vertices of $H$ receive different labels from $[q]$ when $\mathbf{X}\sim\mathsf{L}(n,q).$ This clearly happens with probability

$$ \frac{q-1}{q}\frac{q-2}{q}\cdots\frac{q-|V(H)|}{q}\geq(1-|V(H)|/q)^{|V(H)|}\geq 1-|V(H)|^{2}/q.\qed $$

In light of Eq. 31, it is now useful to bound the differences of Fourier coefficients. Using $\psi_{q}=1/2+o(1)$ and triangle inequality, we obtain the following bound.

#### Proposition 6.5.

For any connected graph $H$ on at most $D$ vertices,

$$ \Big|\Phi^{\psi_{q}}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}(H)-\Phi^{\psi_{q}}_{\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}(H)\Big|\leq 8^{|E(H)|}\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{9}}{q}\Big)^{\max(3,|V(H)|-1)}8^{|E(H)|}\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{9}}{q}\Big)^{3|V(H)|/4}. $$

#### Proof.

We start by writing out the quantity to be bounded,

$$ \begin{split}&\Big|\Phi^{\psi_{q}}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}(H)-\Phi^{\psi_{q}}_{\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}(H)\Big|\\
&=\sqrt{(1-\psi_{q})\psi_{q}}^{-|E(H)|}\Big|\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}}[\mathsf{SW}^{\psi_{q}}_{H}(\mathbf{G})]-\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}[\mathsf{SW}^{\psi_{q}}_{H}(\mathbf{G})]\Big|\\
&\leq 4^{|E(H)|}\Big|\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}}\Big[\prod_{(ji)\in E(H)}\Big(\mathbf{G}_{ji}-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2(q-1)}\Big)\Big]\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad-\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}\Big[\prod_{(ji)\in E(H)}\Big(\mathbf{G}_{ji}-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2(q-1)}\Big)\Big]\Big|\\
&\leq 4^{|E(H)|}\sum_{K\subseteq E(H)}\frac{1}{(2(q-1))^{|E(K)|}}\Big|\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}}\Big[\prod_{(ji)\in E(H)\backslash E(K)}\Big(\mathbf{G}_{ji}-\frac{1}{2}\Big)\Big]\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad-\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}\Big[\prod_{(ji)\in E(H)\backslash E(K)}\Big(\mathbf{G}_{ji}-\frac{1}{2}\Big)\Big]\Big|\\
&=4^{|E(H)|}\sum_{K\subseteq E(H)}\frac{1}{(2(q-1))^{|E(K)|}}\Big|\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}}\Big[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H\backslash E(K)}(\mathbf{G})\Big]-\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}\Big[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H\backslash E(K)}(\mathbf{G})\Big]\Big|\\
&\leq 8^{|E(H)|}\max_{K\subseteq E(H)}\frac{1}{(2(q-1))^{|E(K)|}}\Big|\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}}\Big[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H\backslash E(K)}(\mathbf{G})\Big]-\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}\Big[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H\backslash E(K)}(\mathbf{G})\Big]\Big|.\\
\end{split} $$

Now, we analyze the maximum above. Suppose that $H\backslash E(K)$ has a leaf. Then, both signed expectations equal 0. Hence, we only consider $K$ such that $H\backslash E(K)$ has no leaves. Now, recall the leaf decomposition Definition 10. Clearly, it must be the case that all edges in $\mathsf{TP}(H)$ should be in $K$ so that $H\backslash E(K)$ has no leaves. Note, however, that if $H=\mathsf{TP}(H),$ meaning that $H$ is a tree, $\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}}\Big[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H\backslash E(K)}(\mathbf{G})\Big]-\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}\Big[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H\backslash E(K)}(\mathbf{G})\Big]=0$ holds for all $K$ and, thus, the expression equals zero. Hence, we can assume that $H$ is not a tree. As $H$ is connected, $\mathsf{NLP}(H)\neq\emptyset.$ By Observation 3.3, $|E(\mathsf{TP}(H))|=|V(H)|-|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H))|.$ Denote $A=\mathsf{NLP}(H)\cap K.$

$$ \displaystyle 8^{|E(H)|}\max_{K\subseteq E(H)}\frac{1}{(2(q-1))^{|E(K)|}}\Big|\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}}\Big[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H\backslash E(K)}(\mathbf{G})\Big]-\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}\Big[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H\backslash E(K)}(\mathbf{G})\Big]\Big| \displaystyle\leq 8^{|E(H)|}\max_{K\subseteq E(H)}\frac{1}{q^{|E(A)|+|E(\mathsf{TP}(H))|}}\Big|\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}}\Big[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{\mathsf{NLP}(H)\backslash A}(\mathbf{G})\Big]-\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}\Big[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{\mathsf{NLP}(H)\backslash A}(\mathbf{G})\Big]\Big| \displaystyle\leq 8^{|E(H)|}\max_{A\subseteq\mathsf{NLP}(H)}\frac{1}{q^{|E(A)|+|V(H)|-|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H))|}}\times D\times\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{8}}{q}\Big)^{\max(3,|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H)\backslash A)|-|\mathsf{CC}(\mathsf{NLP}(H)\backslash A)|)} $$

by Proposition 6.2.

Thus, it is enough to show that

$$ |E(A)|+|V(H)|-|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H))|+\max(3,|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H)\backslash A)|-|\mathsf{CC}(\mathsf{NLP}(H)\backslash A)|)\geq\max(3,|V(H)|-1). $$

If $\max(3,|V(H)|-1)=3,$ this means that $H=\triangle$ as otherwise $\mathsf{NLP}(H)=\emptyset.$ In that case, $\mathsf{NLP}(H)=\triangle.$ Thus, the left-hand side is

$$ |E(A)|+\max(3,|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H)\backslash A)|-|\mathsf{CC}(\mathsf{NLP}(H)\backslash A)|)\geq 3, $$

as desired. Otherwise, it is enough to show that

$$ \displaystyle|E(A)|+|V(H)|-|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H))|+|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H)\backslash A)|-|\mathsf{CC}(\mathsf{NLP}(H)\backslash A)|)\geq|V(H)|-1 \displaystyle\Longleftrightarrow|E(A)|+1\geq|\mathsf{CC}(\mathsf{NLP}(H)\backslash A)|+\Big(|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H))|-|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H)\backslash A)|\Big). $$

This, however, is trivial as $\mathsf{NLP}(H)$ is connected whenever $H$ is connected. Furthermore, the graph induced by $V(\mathsf{NLP}(H))$ on edges $\mathsf{NLP}(H)\backslash A$ has connected components $\mathsf{CC}(\mathsf{NLP}(H)\backslash A)$ and $V(\mathsf{NLP}(H))\backslash\Big(V(\mathsf{NLP}(H)\backslash A)\Big).$ Hence, we need to add at least $|\mathsf{CC}(\mathsf{NLP}(H)\backslash A)|+|V(\mathsf{NLP}(H))\backslash\Big(V(\mathsf{NLP}(H)\backslash A)\Big)|-1$ edges to make $\mathsf{NLP}(H)$ on vertex set $V(\mathsf{NLP}(H))$ connected. ∎

Now, we go back to Eq. 31. As we know the difference of Fourier coefficients, we also need to understand the coefficients $M_{K,H}/M_{H,H}.$ We will prove the following fact.

#### Proposition 6.6 ([KVWX23]).

For any graph $H$ on at most $D$ vertices and any $K\subseteq H,$

$$ \frac{M_{K,H}}{M_{K,K}}\leq 4^{|E(H)|-|E(K)|}\times(1/q)^{|V(H)|-|V(K)|}. $$

#### Proof.

We give the proof in [KVWX23] for completeness. Clearly, it is enough to prove the fact for $H$ connected as the bound factorizes over connected components (and the connected components of $K$ form a more refined partitioning of vertices than the components of $H$ ). Now, suppose that $H$ is connected. Then

$$ \displaystyle\frac{M_{K,H}}{M_{K,K}}=\frac{\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[\mathbf{X}|_{E(H)}=E(H)\backslash E(K)]\sqrt{(1-\psi_{q})/\psi_{q}}^{E(H)\backslash E(K)}}{\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[\mathbf{X}|_{E(K)}=\emptyset]} \displaystyle\leq 4^{|E(H)|\backslash E(K)}\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[\mathbf{X}|_{E(H)}=E(H)\backslash E(K)|\mathbf{X}\cap E(K)=\emptyset]\leq 4^{|E(H)|-|E(K)|}(1/{q})^{|V(H)|-|V(K)|}. $$

Each edge in $E(H)\backslash E(K)$ has at least one vertex in $V(H)\backslash V(K).$ As edges in $\mathbf{X}$ are determined by the colors assigned to vertices and $H$ is connected, the event $\mathbf{X}|_{E(H)}=E(H)\backslash E(K)$ (conditioned on the colors of vertices in $V(K)$ ) completely determines the colors of the vertices in $V(H)\backslash V(K).$ Thus, each vertex in $V(H)\backslash V(K)$ can be assigned at most one color. ∎

With all of this, we can readily bound the values of $\widehat{w}_{H}.$ The following proposition from [KVWX23] shows that it is enough to do so for connected graphs. Note that both ${\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}$ and $\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)$ factorize over their connected components. One can easily obtain the following fact:

#### Proposition 6.7.

The values $\widehat{w}_{H}$ factorize over their connected components. That is, if the connected components of $H$ are $H_{1},H_{2},\ldots,H_{t},$ $\widehat{w}_{H}=\prod_{i=1}^{t}\widehat{w}_{H_{i}}.$

#### Proposition 6.8.

For any $H$ on at most $D$ vertices,

$$ |\widehat{w}_{H}|\leq(12|E(H)|)^{|E(H)|}\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{9}}{q}\Big)^{3|V(H)|/4}. $$

#### Proof.

We prove this is by induction on $|E(H)|.$ It clearly holds for $H=\emptyset.$ The left-hand side is multiplicative over disjoint connected components and the right-hand side is super-multiplicative, so we only need to prove the statement for $H$ connected. Now, we use the recurrence relation Eq. 31 as well as the bounds in Propositions 6.5 and 6.6 to obtain

$$ \begin{split}&|\widehat{w}_{H}|=\Big|(\Phi^{\psi_{q}}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}(H)-\Phi^{\psi_{q}}_{\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}(H))-\sum_{\emptyset\subsetneq K\subsetneq H}\widehat{w}_{K}\frac{M_{K,H}}{M_{K,K}}\Big|\\
&\leq|\Phi^{\psi_{q}}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}(H)-\Phi^{\psi_{q}}_{\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}(H))|+\sum_{\emptyset\subsetneq K\subsetneq H}|\widehat{w}_{K}|\frac{M_{K,H}}{M_{K,K}}\\
&\leq 8^{|E(H)|}\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{9}}{q}\Big)^{3|V(H)|/4}\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad+\sum_{\emptyset\subsetneq K\subsetneq H}(12|E(K)|)^{|E(K)|}\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{9}}{q}\Big)^{3|V(K)|/4}4^{|E(H)|-|E(K)|}\Big(\frac{1}{q}\Big)^{|V(H)|-|V(K)|}\\
&\leq\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{9}}{q}\Big)^{3|V(H)|/4}\times\Big(8^{|E(H)|}+\sum_{t=0}^{|E(H)|-1}(12t)^{t}\binom{|E(H)|}{t}4^{|E(H)|-t}\Big)\\
&\leq\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{9}}{q}\Big)^{3|V(H)|/4}\times\Big(8^{|E(H)|}+\sum_{t=0}^{|E(H)|-1}(12(|E(H)|-1))^{t}\binom{|E(H)|}{t}4^{|E(H)|-t}\Big)\\
&\leq\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{9}}{q}\Big)^{3|V(H)|/4}\times\Big(8^{|E(H)|}+(12|E(H)|-8)^{|E(H)|}\Big)\\
&\leq(12|E(H)|)^{|E(H)|}\Big(\frac{(\log n)^{9}}{q}\Big)^{3|V(H)|/4},\end{split} $$

as desired. ∎

These bounds, together with Proposition 6.3 are sufficient via an elementary calculation which we carry out in Section B.2.

## 7 The Second Eigenvalue of Half-Density RGG

### 7.1 The Trace Method

For a real symmetric matrix $A\in\mathbb{(}R)^{n\times n},$ denote by $\lambda_{1}(A),\lambda_{2}(A),\ldots,\lambda_{n}(A)$ its eigenvalues in decreasing order. It is a well known fact that for any symmetric real matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n},$ $\lambda_{2}(A)=\min_{v}\lambda_{1}(A-vv^{T}).$ In particular, if $\mathbf{A}$ is the adjacency matrix of $\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},1/2),$ $\lambda_{2}(\mathbf{A})\leq\lambda_{1}\Big(\mathbf{A}-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{T}\Big).$

Now, we can bound $\lambda_{1}(\mathbf{A}-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{T})$ by the trace method. Namely, let $D$ be any even number.

$$ \sum_{i=1}^{n}\lambda_{i}\Big(\mathbf{A}-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{T}\Big)^{D}=\mathsf{tr}\Big(\Big(\mathbf{A}-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{T}\Big)^{D}\Big). $$

In particular, $|\lambda_{2}(\mathbf{A})|\leq|\lambda_{1}\Big(\mathbf{A}-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{T}\Big)|\leq\mathsf{tr}\Big(\Big(\mathbf{A}-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{T}\Big)^{D}\Big)^{1/D}.$ Hence, by Markov’s inequality,

$$ \frac{1}{n}\geq\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}\Big[\mathsf{tr}\Big(\Big(\mathbf{A}-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{T}\Big)^{D}\Big)\geq n\times\E\Big[\mathsf{tr}\Big(\Big(\mathbf{A}-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{T}\Big)^{D}\Big)\Big]\Big]\geq\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}\Big[|\lambda_{2}(\mathbf{A})|^{D}\geq n\times\E\Big[\mathsf{tr}\Big((\mathbf{A}-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{T})^{D}\Big)\Big]\Big]. $$

Thus, with high probability, $|\lambda_{2}(\mathbf{A})|\leq{n}^{1/D}\times\E\Big[\mathsf{tr}\Big(\Big(\mathbf{A}-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{T}\Big)^{D}\Big)\Big]^{1/D}.$ Taking $D=\omega(\log n),$ with high probability,

$$ |\lambda_{2}(\mathbf{A})|\leq(1+o_{n}(1))\E\Big[\mathsf{tr}\Big(\Big(\mathbf{A}-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{T}\Big)^{D}\Big)\Big]^{1/D}. $$

In the rest of the section, we will be bounding the trace above. We choose $D=2\Big\lceil(\log n)^{1.1}\rceil.$

### 7.2 Fourier Coefficients in The Trace

$\E\Big[\mathsf{tr}\Big(\Big(\mathbf{A}-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{T}\Big)^{D}\Big)\Big]$ has a very convenient expression as a weighted sum of Fourier coefficients.

$$ \begin{split}&\E\Big[\mathsf{tr}\Big(\Big(\mathbf{A}-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{T}\Big)^{D}\Big)\Big]=\\
&=\sum_{1\leq i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D}\leq n}\E\Big[\prod_{s=1}^{D}(A_{i_{s}i_{s+1}}-1/2)\Big]\\
&=\sum_{1\leq i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{m}\leq n}\E\Big[\prod_{s=1}^{D}(G_{i_{s}i_{s+1}}-1/2)\Big]\Longrightarrow\\
&\Big|\E\Big[\mathsf{tr}\Big(\Big(\mathbf{A}-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{T}\Big)^{D}\Big)\Big]\Big|\leq\sum_{1\leq i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D}\leq n}\Big|\E\Big[\prod_{s=1}^{D}(G_{i_{s}i_{s+1}}-1/2)\Big]\Big|,\end{split} $$

where $i_{D+1}:=i_{1}.$ Now, observe that for any indicator $I,$ one has $(I-1/2)^{2}=1/4.$ Thus, relevant are only terms that appear an odd number of times. Explicitly, let $H(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D})$ be the graph induced by the edges appearing an odd number of times in the multiset $\{(i_{1},i_{2}),(i_{2},i_{3}),\ldots,(i_{D},i_{1})\}.$ Then, Eq. 34 is upper bounded by

$$ \begin{split}&\sum_{1\leq i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D}\leq n}\E[\mathsf{SW}_{H(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D})}(\mathbf{G})]|=\sum_{H\in\mathcal{NLG}_{D}}|\E[\mathsf{SW}_{H}(\mathbf{G})]|\times f_{D,n}(H),\end{split} $$

where $f_{D,n}(H)$ is the number of $D$ -tuples in $[n]^{D}$ such that $H(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D})$ is isomorphic to $H.$ Again, we only sum over graphs with no leaves.

### 7.3 Bounding The Trace

We first bound $f_{D,n}(H).$

#### Proposition 7.1.

Suppose that $H$ is of minimal degree $2.$ Then,

$$ f_{D,n}(H)\leq 2D^{3D}n^{|V(H)|-|\mathsf{CC}(H)|+(D-|E(H)|)/2+1} $$

#### Proof.

For $i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D},$ denote by $K(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D})$ the multigraph on vertices $i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D}$ with edges $\{(i_{1},i_{2}),(i_{2},i_{3}),\ldots,(i_{D},i_{1})\}$ (counted with multiplicities).

First, we claim that $K(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D})$ has at most $D-|E(H)|$ vertices if $H(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D})=H.$ Indeed, consider the graph $K^{c}(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D})$ in which one modifies $K(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D})$ by contracting each connected component of $H(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D})$ to a single vertex. Then, the resulting multigraph has exactly $D-|E(H)|$ edges, is connected as $K$ clearly is, and each edge is of even multiplicity. In particular, this means that $|V(K^{c}(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D}))|\leq(D-|E(H)|)/2+1.$ However,

$$ |V(K(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D}))|=|V(K(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D}))|+|V(H)|-|\mathsf{CC}(H)|\leq|V(H)|-|\mathsf{CC}(H)|+(D-|E(H)|)/2+1. $$

Hence, one can choose the vertices $i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D}$ in at most

$$ \sum_{t=|V(H)|}^{|V(H)|-|\mathsf{CC}(H)|+(D-|E(H)|)/2+1}n^{t}\leq 2n^{|V(H)|-|\mathsf{CC}(H)|+(D-|E(H)|)/2+1} $$

ways. On the other hand, for each fixed choice of $V(K(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D})),$ one needs to add an extra $(D-|E(H)|)/2$ double edges besides the ones determined by $H(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D}).$ As $|V(K(i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D}))|\leq D,$ this can be done in at most

$$ \sum_{t=0}^{D}\binom{\binom{t}{2}}{D}\leq\binom{D^{2}}{D}\leq D^{2D} $$

ways. Finally, note that for each fixed $K=K(i_{1},\ldots,i_{D}),$ there are at most $D^{D}$ walks on the vertices $i_{1},i_{2},\ldots,i_{D}.$ ∎

We now bound $|\mathsf{SW}_{H}(\mathbf{G})|.$ First, from Theorems 1.1 and 1.2,

$$ |\E[\mathsf{SW}_{H}(\mathbf{G})]|\leq\Big((\log n)^{4}/\sqrt{d}\Big)^{\sum_{H_{i}\in\mathsf{CC}(H)}\lceil(|V(H_{i})|-1)/2\rceil}. $$

Second, by Propositions 1.3 and 1.4,

$$ |\E[\mathsf{SW}_{H}(\mathbf{G})]|\leq\Big((\log n)^{4}/\sqrt{d}\Big)^{\sum_{H_{i}\in\mathsf{CC}(H)}\Big(2|V(H_{i})|-|E(H_{i})|-2\Big)}. $$

Hence, if we define $\mu(A):=\max\Big(\lceil(|V(A)|-1)/2\rceil,2|V(A)|-|E(A)|-2\Big),$ we obtain

$$ \begin{split}&|\E[\mathsf{SW}_{H}(\mathbf{G})]|\leq\Big((\log n)^{4}/\sqrt{d}\Big)^{\sum_{H_{i}\in\mathsf{CC}(H)}\mu(H_{i})}.\\
\end{split} $$

Now, we go back to Eq. 34.

$$ \begin{split}&\sum_{H\in\mathcal{NLG}_{D}}|\E[\mathsf{SW}_{H}(\mathbf{G})]|\times f_{D,n}(H)\\
&\leq\sum_{H\in\mathcal{NLG}_{D}}2D^{3D}n^{|V(H)|-|\mathsf{CC}(H)|+(D-|E(H)|)/2+1}\prod_{H_{i}\in\mathsf{CC}(H)}\Big((\log n)^{4}/\sqrt{d}\Big)^{\mu(H_{i})}\\
&=2D^{3D}n^{D/2+1}\sum_{H\in\mathcal{NLG}_{D}}\prod_{H_{i}\in\mathsf{CC}(H)}n^{|V(H_{i})|-|E(H_{i})|/2-1}\Big((\log n)^{4}/\sqrt{d}\Big)^{\mu(H_{i})}\\
&=2D^{3D}n^{D/2+1}\sum_{H\in\mathcal{NLG}_{D}}\prod_{H_{i}\in\mathsf{CC}(H)}n^{(2|V(H_{i})|-|E(H_{i})|-2)/2}\times n^{|V(H_{i})|/2}\Big((\log n)^{4}/\sqrt{d}\Big)^{\mu(H_{i})}\\
&\leq 2D^{3D}n^{D/2+2}\sum_{H\in\mathcal{NLG}_{D}}\prod_{H_{i}\in\mathsf{CC}(H)}\Big(\sqrt{n}(\log n)^{4}/\sqrt{d}\Big)^{\mu(H_{i})}\\
&\leq 2D^{5D}n^{D/2+2}\max_{H\in\mathcal{NLG}_{D}}\prod_{H_{i}\in\mathsf{CC}(H)}\Big(\sqrt{n}(\log n)^{4}/\sqrt{d}\Big)^{\mu(H_{i})}.\end{split} $$

For the last line, we simply counted the number of graphs $H$ on at most $D$ edges and $D$ vertices. Summing first over vertices and then edges, one can bound

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{v=1}^{D}\sum_{1\leq e\leq\max(\binom{v}{2},D)}\binom{\binom{v}{2}}{e}\leq\sum_{v=1}^{D}D\min\Big(2^{\binom{v}{2}},\binom{\binom{v}{2}}{D}\Big)\leq D^{2}\binom{\binom{D}{2}}{D}\leq D^{2D}. $$

The last line of Eq. 37 clearly suggests two cases.

#### Case 1)

If $d\leq n(\log n)^{8}.$ Then, the expression is maximized when $\sum_{H_{i}\in\mathsf{CC}(H)}\mu(H_{i})$ is maximized. As $\mu(H_{i})\leq|V(H_{i})|$ holds, $\sum_{H_{i}\in\mathsf{CC}(H)}\mu(H_{i})\leq|V(H)|\leq|V(H)|=D.$ Going back to Eq. 33,

$$ \displaystyle|\lambda_{2}(\mathbf{A})|\leq\Big(2D^{5D}n^{D/2+2}\Big(\sqrt{n}(\log n)^{4}/\sqrt{d}\Big)^{D}\Big)^{1/D}\leq(\log n)^{10}n/\sqrt{d}. $$

#### Case 2)

If $d\geq n(\log n)^{8},$ then the expression is maximized when $\sum_{H_{i}\in\mathsf{CC}(H)}\mu(H_{i})$ is minimized. As $\mu(H_{i})\geq 0,$

$$ \displaystyle|\lambda_{2}(\mathbf{A})|\leq\Big(2D^{5D}n^{D/2+2}\Big)^{1/D}\leq(\log n)^{10}\sqrt{n}. $$

## 8 Discussion

We introduced a novel strategy for bounding the Fourier coefficients of graph distributions with high-dimensional latent geometry. It is based on localizing dependence to few edges and applying a noise operator to (some of) the remaining edges. Not only is this method useful for our concrete goal of bounding Fourier coefficients, but it also explains how and where dependence among edges is created. In the setting of ${\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)},{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},p)},$ dependence is localized to fragile edges. For them, the signal $Z_{ji}$ is too low to overwhelm the bias $\sum_{\ell<i}Z_{i\ell}Z_{j\ell}$ introduced by other edges. We also showed that fragile edges give rise to an energy-entropy trade-off phenomenon in $\mathsf{RGG}$ (see Remark 6). We anticipate future applications of the fragile edges approach.

One future direction is tightening our bounds on the Fourier coefficients. In particular, proving a bound based on $\mathsf{SOEI}$ as in Proposition 1.3 for all densities is appealing as it will extend Theorem 1.9 to all densities. Can one improve further or is Proposition 1.3 tight (up to lower-order terms)?

We used our bounds in several contexts related to low-degree hardness. The information-theoretic counterparts of many of these questions remain open. Is it possible to prove such information theoretic convergence using $\chi^{2}$ -like arguments based on squares of Fourier coefficients? A simple calculation shows that bounds scaling as $p^{|E(H)|}d^{-\theta|V(H)|}$ for constant $\theta$ (of which form Theorems 1.1 and 1.3 both are) are insufficient to show $\chi^{2}({\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},p)}\|\mathsf{G}(n,p))=o_{n}(1)$ as there are $\exp(\omega(|V(H)|(\log d)))$ copies of $H$ in $K_{n}$ when $|V(H)|=\omega(\log^{2}n).$ Nevertheless, one could potentially use a tensorization argument first to reduce the computation to distributions over a smaller number of edges, for example as in [LR23, LMSY22].

Finally, we separated sparse Gaussian and spherical random geometric graphs. It seems worthwhile to analyse this discrepancy further. First, it suggests that different methods are needed for studying their information-theoretic convergence to Erdős-Rényi in the regime $1/n\ll p\ll 1/2.$ Second, to what extent do sparse Gaussian random geometric graphs enjoy properties of their spherical counterparts such as high-dimensional expansion [LMSY23]?

### A.1 Variance of The Signed Wedge Count in The Unmasked Case

Going through the same steps as in the Erdős-Rényi case, one can show that

$$ \mathsf{Var}_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{RGG}}[\mathsf{SW}_{\wedge(1,2,3)}(\mathbf{G})]=(p-p^{2})^{2}+(1-2p)^{2}\E[(G_{12}-p)(G_{13}-p)]\leq p^{2}+\frac{p^{2}(\log d)^{4}}{d}\leq 2p^{2} $$

for large enough $d$ by Proposition 3.3. So far the contribution to the variance is $O(n^{3}p^{2}).$ Next, we analyze the covariances based on the overlap pattern.

#### Case 2.1) Overlap of zero vertices.

That is, $\wedge(1,2,3)$ and $\wedge(4,5,6).$ Those are clearly independent as they are determined by a disjoint set of latent vectors, so the covariance is $0.$

#### Case 2.2) Overlap of one vertex.

There are several possible patterns: $\wedge(1,2,3)$ and $\wedge(1,4,5);$ $\wedge(1,2,3)$ and $\wedge(4,2,5);$ $\wedge(1,2,3)$ and $\wedge(4,1,5).$ Importantly, in all three cases, when we take the union of the two wedges we get a tree $T$ with $4$ edges. Thus,

$$ \displaystyle\mathsf{Cov}[\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{\wedge(i,j,k)},\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{\wedge(i^{\prime},j^{\prime},k^{\prime})}] \displaystyle=\E_{G\sim\mathsf{RGG}}[\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{T}(\mathbf{G})]-\E_{G\sim\mathsf{RGG}}[\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{\wedge(1,2,3)}(\mathbf{G})]^{2} \displaystyle\leq\E_{G\sim\mathsf{RGG}}[\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{T}(\mathbf{G})]\leq\frac{p^{4}}{d^{2}}\times(\log d)^{8}, $$

where we used Proposition 3.3 for a tree on 4 edges. As there are $O(n^{5})$ ways to choose the tree $T$ as it has 5 vertices, the contribution to the variance is of order $\tilde{O}({n^{5}p^{4}}/{d^{2}}).$

#### Case 2.3) Overlap of two vertices.

We analyze several different patterns separately:

#### Case 2.3.1)

$\wedge(1,2,3)$ and $\wedge(1,2,4).$ Then,

$$ \begin{split}&\E[\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{\wedge(1,2,3)}(\mathbf{G})\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{\wedge(1,2,4)}(\mathbf{G})]\\
&=\E[(G_{12}-p)^{2}(G_{13}-p)(G_{14-p})]\\
&=(1-2p)\E[(G_{12}-p)(G_{13}-p)(G_{14}-p)]+(p-p^{2})\E[(G_{13}-p)(G_{14}-p)]\\
&=\tilde{O}(p^{3}/d^{3/2}+p^{3}/d)={O}((\log d)^{6}p^{3}/d),\end{split} $$

where we used Proposition 3.3 for the trees defined by edges $(12),(13)$ and $(12),(13),(14).$ Thus, the contribution is $O((\log d)^{6}n^{4}p^{3}/d).$

#### Case 2.3.2)

$\wedge(1,2,3)$ and $\wedge(2,1,4).$ Then,

$$ \begin{split}&\E[\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{\wedge(1,2,3)}(\mathbf{G})\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{\wedge(2,1,4)}(\mathbf{G})]\\
&=\E[(G_{12}-p)^{2}(G_{13}-p)(G_{24}-p)]\\
&=(1-2p)\E[(G_{12}-p)(G_{13}-p)(G_{24}-p)]+(p-p^{2})\E[(G_{13}-p)(G_{24-p})]\\
&=O((\log d)^{6}(p^{3}/d^{3/2}+p^{3}/d))=O((\log d)^{6}p^{3}/d),\end{split} $$

where we used Proposition 3.3 for the trees defined by edges $(12),(13)$ and $(12),(13),(24).$ Thus, the contribution is $O((\log d)^{6}n^{4}p^{3}/d).$

#### Case 2.3.3)

$\wedge(1,2,3)$ and $\wedge(4,2,3).$ Then,

$$ \begin{split}&\E[\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{\wedge(1,2,3)}(\mathbf{G})\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{\wedge(4,2,3)}(\mathbf{G})]\\
&=\E[(G_{12}-p)(G_{13}-p)(G_{24}-p)(G_{34}-p)]\\
&=O((\log d)^{6}(p^{3}/d^{3/2}+p^{4}/d^{2}))=O((\log d)^{6}p^{4}/d^{2}),\end{split} $$

where we used Theorem 1.1 and Proposition 1.2 for the 4-cycle graph. The contribution is $\tilde{O}(n^{4}p^{4}/d^{2}).$

#### Case 2.4) Overlap of 3 vertices.

There are two patterns - $\wedge(1,2,3)$ and $\wedge(1,2,3),$ which is the variance case and $\wedge(1,2,3)$ and $\wedge(2,1,3).$ In the latter case,

$$ \begin{split}&\E[\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{\wedge(1,2,3)}(\mathbf{G})\mathsf{SW}^{p}_{\wedge(2,1,3)}(\mathbf{G})]\\
&=\E[(G_{12}-p)^{2}(G_{13}-p)(G_{23}-p)]\\
&=(1-2p)\E[(G_{12}-p)(G_{13}-p)(G_{23}-p)]+(p-p^{2})\E[(G_{13}-p)(G_{23}-p)]\\
&=O((\log d)^{4}(p^{3}/d^{1/2}+p^{3}/d))=O((\log d)^{4}p^{3}/d^{1/2}),\end{split} $$

by Proposition 3.3 for the triangle $(12),(23),(13)$ and the wedge $(13),(23).$ Thus, the contribution is $O((\log d)^{4}n^{3}p^{3}/d^{1/2}).$

Since $\E_{G\sim\mathsf{RGG}}[\mathsf{CS}^{p}_{\wedge}(\mathbf{G})]-\E_{H\sim\mathsf{G}(n,p)}[\mathsf{CS}^{p}_{\wedge}(H)]=\tilde{\Omega}(n^{3}p^{2}/d),$ for the signed wedge count test to distinguish the two models with high probability, it is sufficient that

$$ n^{6}p^{4}/((\log d)^{8}d^{2})=\omega\Big((\log d)^{8}\times\Big(n^{3}p^{2}+n^{5}p^{4}/d^{2}+n^{4}p^{3}/d+n^{4}p^{4}/d^{2}\Big)\Big). $$

We analyze the inequalities separately:

- 1. $n^{6}p^{4}/d^{2}=\omega\Big((\log d)^{16}n^{3}p^{2}\Big).$ This holds if and only if $d=o(n^{3/2}p(\log d)^{-8}).$

- 2. $n^{6}p^{4}/d^{2}=\omega\Big((\log d)^{16}n^{5}p^{4}/d^{2}\Big).$ This holds for all $d,1/p$ under (A).

- 3. $n^{6}p^{4}/d^{2}=\omega\Big((\log d)^{16}Cn^{4}p^{3}/d\Big).$ This holds if and only if $d=o(n^{2}p(\log d)^{-16}).$

- 4. $n^{6}p^{4}/d^{2}=\omega\Big((\log d)^{16}n^{4}p^{4}/d^{2}\Big).$ This holds for all $d,1/p$ under (A).

Altogether, whenever $d=o(n^{3/2}p(\log d)^{-8}),$ the signed-wedge test distinguishes the two graph models with high probability.

### A.2 Variance of The Signed Triangle Count in The Unmasked Case

#### Case 2.1) Overlap of zero vertices.

That is $\triangle(1,2,3)$ and $\triangle(2,3,4)$ are clearly independent.

$\triangle(1,2,3)$ and $\triangle(1,4,5).$ Then,

#### Case 2.2) Overlap of two vertices.

$\triangle(1,2,3)$ and $\triangle(1,2,4).$ Then,

$$ \begin{split}&\E[\mathsf{SW}_{\triangle(1,2,3)}(\mathbf{G})\mathsf{SW}_{\triangle(1,2,4)}(\mathbf{G})]\\
&=\E[(G_{12}-p)^{2}(G_{13}-p)(G_{23}-p)(G_{14}-p)(G_{24}-p)]\\

where we used Theorem 1.1 and Proposition 1.2 on the 4-cycle and the graph with $4$ vertices and 5 edges. The contribution is $O(n^{4}p^{5}(\log d)^{4}/d).$

#### Case 2.3) Overlap of three vertices.

$\triangle(1,2,3)$ and $\triangle(1,2,3).$ Then,

$$ \begin{split}&\E[\mathsf{SW}_{\triangle(1,2,3)}(\mathbf{G})\mathsf{SW}_{\triangle(1,2,3)}(\mathbf{G})]\\
&=\E[(G_{12}-p)^{2}(G_{13}-p)^{2}(G_{23}-p)^{2}]\\
&=(1-2p)^{3}\E[(G_{12}-p)(G_{13}-p)(G_{23}-p)]+3(1-2p)(p-p^{2})\E[(G_{12}-p)(G_{13}-p)]\\
&\quad\quad\quad+3(1-2p)(p-p^{2})\E[(G_{12}-p)]+(p-p^{2})^{3}\\
&=O(p^{3}),\end{split} $$

where we used Theorem 1.1 and Proposition 1.2 on the triangle and Proposition 3.3 for the wedge. The total contribution is $O(n^{3}p^{3}).$

Finally, in light of Definition 8, we have to show

$$ n^{6}p^{6}(\log d)^{-2}/d=\omega\Big(n^{5}p^{6}(\log d)^{4}/d+n^{4}p^{5}(\log d)^{4}/d+n^{3}p^{3}\Big) $$

This clearly holds whenever $d\leq(n^{3}p^{3})(\log d)^{-2}.$

### A.4 Lower Bound on Expected Signed Wedges in Gaussian RGG

#### Proof of Lemma 3.2.

To prove this statement, we decompose each Gaussian vector $Z_{i}$ as $V_{i}\times\|Z_{i}\|_{2},$ where $V_{i}\sim\mathsf{Unif}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})$ and $d\|Z_{i}\|^{2}\sim\chi^{2}(d).$ Importantly, $V_{i}$ and $\|Z_{i}\|_{2}$ are independent. In this decomposition, $\langle V_{1},V_{3}\rangle$ and $\langle V_{1},V_{2}\rangle$ are independent, unlike $\langle Z_{1},Z_{2}\rangle.$ We use the independence in the same way as in Proposition 3.2.

$$ \begin{split}&\E\Big[(G_{21}-p)(G_{31}-p)\Big]\\
&=\E\Big[\Big(\mathds{1}\Big[\langle V_{1},V_{2}\rangle\geq\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{\|Z_{1}\|_{2}\times\|Z_{2}\|_{2}}\Big]-p\Big)\times\Big(\mathds{1}\Big[\langle V_{1},V_{3}\rangle\geq\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{\|Z_{1}\|_{2}\times\|Z_{3}\|_{2}}\Big]-p\Big)\Big]\\
&=\E\Big[\E\Big[\Big(\mathds{1}\Big[\langle V_{1},V_{2}\rangle\geq\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{\|Z_{1}\|_{2}\times\|Z_{2}\|_{2}}\Big]-p\Big)\times\Big(\mathds{1}\Big[\langle V_{1},V_{3}\rangle\geq\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{\|Z_{1}\|_{2}\times\|Z_{3}\|_{2}}\Big]-p\Big)\;\Big|\;\|Z_{1}\|_{2}\Big]\Big]\\
&=\E\Big[\E\Big[\Big(\mathds{1}\Big[\langle V_{1},V_{2}\rangle\geq\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{\|Z_{1}\|_{2}\times\|Z_{2}\|_{2}}\Big]-p\Big)\Big|\|Z_{1}\|\Big]^{2}\Big].\end{split} $$

For brevity denote $h(x):=\E\Big[\Big(\mathds{1}\Big[\langle V_{1},V_{2}\rangle\geq\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{x\times\|Z_{2}\|_{2}}\Big]-p\Big)\Big].$ We know that $\E[h(\|Z_{1}\|)]=0$ by definition of $\rho^{p}_{d}.$ Also, we can rewrite Eq. 46 as $\E[h(\|Z_{1}\|)^{2}].$

Now, by $\chi$ -square concentration, the median of $\|Z_{1}\|$ is $1+\frac{m}{\sqrt{d}}$ where $|m|\leq 20.$ Indeed, this holds by setting $y=8/\sqrt{d}$ in Proposition 3.5.

Now, using the chi-squared density, one can easily prove that $\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[\|Z_{1}\|\geq 1+\frac{(m+1)}{\sqrt{d}}]\geq C$ for some absolute constant $C.$ On the one hand, $\|Z_{1}\|_{2}\in[1-10/\sqrt{d},1+\sqrt{10}/d]$ with constant probability by Proposition 3.5. On the other hand, the density of $\|Z_{1}\|_{2}$ on $[1+\frac{21}{\sqrt{d}},\frac{22}{\sqrt{d}}]$ is not that much smaller than the density on $[(1-10/\sqrt{d}),(1+\sqrt{10}/d)],$ hence also a constant fraction of the mass of $\|Z_{1}\|_{2}$ is in $[1+\frac{21}{\sqrt{d}},\frac{22}{\sqrt{d}}].$ Formally, the density $f_{d}(v)$ of $\|Z_{1}\|^{2}$ is given by

$$ f_{d}(v)=\frac{1}{2^{d/2}\Gamma(d/2)}(dv)^{d/2-1}e^{-(dv)/2}. $$

However, whenever $\|Z_{1}\|_{2}\in[1-10/\sqrt{d},1+\sqrt{10}/d]$ holds, $\|Z_{1}\|^{2}_{2}\in[1-21/\sqrt{d},1+\sqrt{21}/d]$ holds and whenever $\|Z_{1}\|_{2}\in[1+\frac{21}{\sqrt{d}},\frac{22}{\sqrt{d}}]$ holds, $\|Z_{1}\|_{2}\in[1+\frac{40}{\sqrt{d}},\frac{44}{\sqrt{d}}]$ holds. However, for any $a\in[-21,21],b\in[40,44],$ one has

$$ \begin{split}&\frac{f_{d}(1+\frac{b}{d})}{f_{d}(1-\frac{a}{d})}=\Big(\frac{1+\frac{b}{\sqrt{d}}}{1-\frac{a}{\sqrt{d}}}\Big)^{d/2-1}e^{-(b-a)\sqrt{d}/2}\\
&\geq\frac{1}{2}\Big(\Big(\frac{1+\frac{b}{\sqrt{d}}}{1-\frac{a}{\sqrt{d}}}\Big)^{\sqrt{d}}e^{-(b-a)}\Big)^{\sqrt{d}/2}\geq\frac{1}{2}\Big(\Big(\frac{1+\frac{b}{\sqrt{d}}}{1-\frac{a}{\sqrt{d}}}\Big)^{\sqrt{d}}\Big(1-\frac{(b-a)}{\sqrt{d}-(b-a)}\Big)^{\sqrt{d}}\Big)^{\sqrt{d}/2}\\
&=\frac{1}{2}\Big(\Big(\frac{d+(2a-b)\sqrt{d}-2b(b-a)}{d+(2a-b)\sqrt{d}+a(b-a)}\Big)\Big)^{d/2}\geq\exp(-10(2b-a)(b-a))=\Omega(1),\end{split} $$

where in the last line we just used $(1-x/n)^{n}\geq\exp(-10x)$ for all large enough $x.$ This is enough as $a,b$ are both at most $44$ in absolute value.

Going back, this means that

$$ \begin{split}&\E\Big[(G_{21}-p)(G_{31}-p)\Big]=\E[h(\|Z_{1}\|)^{2}]\\
&\geq\E\Big[h(\|Z_{1}\|)^{2}\Big|\|Z_{1}\|_{2}\geq 1+\frac{(m+1)}{\sqrt{d}}\Big]\times\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}\Big[\|Z_{1}\|_{2}\geq 1+\frac{(m+1)}{\sqrt{d}}\Big]\\
&\geq C\times\E\Big[h(\|Z_{1}\|)\Big|\|Z_{1}\|_{2}\geq 1+\frac{(m+1)}{\sqrt{d}}\Big]^{2}\\
\end{split} $$

Now, observe that since $h$ is clearly increasing, one has

$$ \begin{split}&\E\Big[h(\|Z_{1}\|)\Big|\|Z_{1}\|_{2}\geq 1+\frac{(m+1)}{\sqrt{d}}\Big]\geq\E\Big[h(\|Z_{1}\|)\Big|\|Z_{1}\|_{2}\geq 1+\frac{m}{\sqrt{d}}\Big],\\
&\E\Big[h(\|Z_{1}\|)\Big|\|Z_{1}\|_{2}\geq 1+\frac{(m+1)}{\sqrt{d}}\Big]\geq\E\Big[h(\|Z_{1}\|+\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}})\Big|\|Z_{1}\|_{2}<1+\frac{m}{\sqrt{d}}\Big].\end{split} $$

Using the concentration of $\|Z_{2}\|$ and $\|Z_{1}\|,$ we can show that

$$ \E\Big[h(\|Z_{1}\|+\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}})\Big|\|Z_{1}\|_{2}<1+\frac{m}{\sqrt{d}}\Big]\geq\E\Big[h(\|Z_{1}\|)\Big|\|Z_{1}\|_{2}<1+\frac{m}{\sqrt{d}}\Big]+\frac{p\times(\log d)^{-2})}{\sqrt{d}}. $$

Indeed, this is true for the following reason. With probability $1-\exp(-(\log d)^{2}),$ both of $\|Z\|_{1}$ and $\|Z_{2}\|_{2}$ are of order $1+O(\log d/\sqrt{d}),$ even conditioned on $\|Z\|_{1}<1+m/\sqrt{d}$ since this latter event has probability $1/2.$ However, whenever this occurs, one has

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{\|Z_{1}\|\times\|Z_{2}\|}-\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{(\|Z_{1}\|+\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}})\times\|Z_{2}\|}=\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{\|Z_{1}\|\times\|Z_{2}\|\times((\|Z_{1}\|+\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}))}\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\geq\frac{K\sqrt{\log d}}{{d}} $$

for some absolute constant $K.$ We used $p\leq 1/2-\varepsilon$ so that $\rho^{p}_{d}\gtrsim 1/\sqrt{d}.$ This is enough to show that

$$ \,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}\Big[\langle V_{1},V_{2}\rangle\geq\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{(\|Z_{1}\|+\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}})\times\|Z_{2}\|}\Big]-\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}\Big[\langle V_{1},V_{2}\rangle\geq\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{\|Z_{1}\|\times\|Z_{2}\|}\Big]\geq\frac{p(\log d)^{-2}}{\sqrt{d}} $$

by Corollary 3.6. Finally, Eq. 50 implies the following bound.

$$ \begin{split}&\E\Big[h(\|Z_{1}\|)\Big|\|Z_{1}\|_{2}\geq 1+\frac{(m+1)}{\sqrt{d}}\Big]\\
&\geq\frac{1}{2}\Big(\E\Big[h(\|Z_{1}\|)\Big|\|Z_{1}\|_{2}\geq 1+\frac{m}{\sqrt{d}}\Big]+\E\Big[h(\|Z_{1}\|)\Big|\|Z_{1}\|_{2}<1+\frac{m}{\sqrt{d}}\Big]+\frac{p\times(\log d)^{-2}}{\sqrt{d}}\Big)\\
&=\E\Big[h(\|Z_{1}\|)\Big]+\frac{p\times(\log d)^{-2}}{\sqrt{d}}=\frac{p\times(\log d)^{-2}}{\sqrt{d}}.\\
\end{split} $$

Going back to Eq. 48, this gives the desired result. ∎

### A.5 Lower Bound on Expected Signed Triangles in Gaussian RGG

#### Proof of Lemma 5.1.

First, note that

$$ \begin{split}&\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}}\Big[(G_{21}-p)(G_{32}-p)(G_{31}-p)\Big]\\
&\E[G_{21}G_{32}G_{31}]-p^{3}\\
&\quad\quad\quad-\Big(p\E[(G_{21}-p)(G_{31}-p)]+p\E[(G_{21}-p)(G_{32}-p)]+p\E[(G_{31}-p)(G_{31}-p)]\Big)\\
&\quad\quad\quad-\Big(p^{2}\E[(G_{21}-p)]+p^{2}\E[(G_{31}-p)]+p^{2}\E[(G_{32}-p)]\Big).\end{split} $$

By Lemma A.1, the expression in the first brackets is on the order of $\tilde{O}(p^{3}/d).$ the expression in the second brackets it is trivially zero. Thus, we simply need to show that

$$ \E[G_{21}G_{32}G_{31}]-p^{3}=\Omega(p^{3}(\log d)^{-1}/\sqrt{d}). $$

Now, observe that

$$ \displaystyle\E[G_{21}G_{32}G_{31}] \displaystyle=\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[\langle Z_{3},Z_{2}\rangle\geq\rho^{p}_{d},\langle Z_{1},Z_{2}\rangle\geq\rho^{p}_{d},\langle Z_{1},Z_{3}\rangle\geq\rho^{p}_{d}] \displaystyle\geq\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[\langle Z_{3},Z_{2}\rangle\geq\rho^{p}_{d},\langle Z_{1},Z_{2}\rangle\geq\rho^{p/2}_{d},\langle Z_{1},Z_{3}\rangle\geq\rho^{p/2}_{d}] \displaystyle=\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[\langle Z_{3},Z_{2}\rangle\geq\rho^{p}_{d}|\langle Z_{1},Z_{2}\rangle\geq\rho^{p/2}_{d},\langle Z_{1},Z_{3}\rangle\geq\rho^{p/2}_{d}]\times\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[\langle Z_{1},Z_{2}\rangle\geq\rho^{p/2}_{d},\langle Z_{1},Z_{3}\rangle\geq\rho^{p/2}_{d}]. $$

Lemma 3.2 shows that $G_{21},G_{31}$ are positively correlated, hence $\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[\langle Z_{1},Z_{2}\rangle\geq\rho^{p/2}_{d},\langle Z_{1},Z_{3}\rangle\geq\rho^{p/2}_{d}]\geq p^{2}/4.$ Using the Bartlett decomposition, we are left to bound

$$ \,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[Z_{22}Z_{32}+Z_{21}Z_{31}\geq\rho^{p}_{d}|Z_{11}Z_{21}\geq\rho^{p/2}_{d},Z_{11}Z_{31}\geq\rho^{p/2}_{d}]. $$

Now, we use that with probability at least $1-\exp(-(\log d)^{2}),$ one has $Z_{11}\leq 1+O(\frac{\log d}{d})\leq 2.$ Thus, we have that

$$ \displaystyle\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[Z_{22}Z_{32}+Z_{21}Z_{31}\geq\rho^{p}_{d}|Z_{11}Z_{21}\geq\rho^{p/2}_{d},Z_{11}Z_{31}\geq\rho^{p/2}_{d}] \displaystyle\geq\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[Z_{22}Z_{32}+Z_{21}Z_{31}\geq\rho^{p}_{d}|Z_{11}Z_{21}\geq\rho^{p/2}_{d},Z_{11}Z_{31}\geq\rho^{p/2}_{d},Z_{11}\leq 2]-\exp(-(\log d)^{2}) \displaystyle\geq\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[Z_{22}Z_{32}\geq\rho^{p}_{d}-\frac{(\rho^{p/2}_{d})^{2}}{4}]-\exp(-(\log d)^{2}) \displaystyle=\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}\Big[Z_{22}Z_{32}\geq\rho^{p}_{d}\Big]+\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}\Big[Z_{22}Z_{32}\in\Big[\rho^{p}_{d}-\frac{(\rho^{p/2}_{d})^{2}}{4},\rho^{p}_{d}\Big]\Big]-\exp(-(\log d)^{2}). $$

Finally, note that $\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}\Big[Z_{22}Z_{32}\geq\rho^{p}_{d}\Big]=\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}\Big[Z_{11}Z_{31}\geq\rho^{p}_{d}\Big]=p.$ However, $\frac{(\rho^{p/2}_{d})^{2}}{4}\geq\frac{(\log d)^{-1}}{d}$ (this is the reason we used $\rho^{p/2}_{d}.$ When $p=1/2,$ one has $\rho^{1/2}_{d}=0$ ). The result follows from Corollary 3.6.∎

### A.6 Upper Bound on Expected Signed Graphs with Leaves in Gaussian RGG

We begin by analyzing the simplest case of graphs with leaves - that of trees.

#### Lemma A.1 (Signed Expectations of Trees).

Suppose that $T$ is a tree with $t$ vertices $[t]$ such that $v=|V(T)|\leq d(\log d)^{-4}.$ Let $\mathcal{E}$ be the event that $\Big|\|Z_{i}\|_{2}-1\Big|=\psi_{i},$ where each $\psi_{i}$ is some constant satisfying $|\psi_{i}|\leq\frac{A\log d}{\sqrt{d}}$ holds for all $i\in[t]$ for some $A$ such that $\sqrt{d}(\log d)^{-2}\geq A\geq C\sqrt{|V(T)|}$ for some absolute constant $C.$ Then,

$$ \displaystyle\Big|\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}}\Big[\prod_{(ji)\in E(T)}(G_{ji}-p)\Big|\mathcal{E}\Big]\Big|\leq\Big(\frac{pA(\log d)^{2}}{\sqrt{d}}\Big)^{|E(T)|}, \displaystyle\Big|\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{1}{d}I_{d}),p)}}\Big[\prod_{(ji)\in E(T)}(G_{ji}-p)\Big]\Big|\leq\Big(\frac{Cp\sqrt{|V(T)|}(\log d)^{2}}{\sqrt{d}}\Big)^{|E(T)|}. $$

#### Proof.

Suppose that $V(T)=\{1,2,\ldots,t\}.$ Let $Z_{1},Z_{2},\ldots,Z_{t}$ be the latent Gaussian vectors. Let $V_{i}=Z_{i}/\|Z_{i}\|_{2}.$ Note that $V_{i}$ and $\|Z_{i}\|_{2}$ are independent as in Lemma 3.2. Again, we write,

$$ \begin{split}&\E\Big[\prod_{(ji)\in E(T)}(G_{ji}-p)\Big|{\mathcal{E}}\Big]\\
&=\E\Big[\prod_{(ji)\in E(T)}\Big(\mathds{1}\Big[\langle V_{i},V_{j}\rangle\geq\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{\|Z_{i}\|_{2}\times\|Z_{j}\|_{2}}\Big]-p\Big)\Big|{\|Z_{i}\|_{2}=\psi_{i}\;\forall i}\Big]\\
&=\E\Big[\E\Big[\prod_{(ji)\in E(T)}\Big(\mathds{1}\Big[\langle V_{i},V_{j}\rangle\geq\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{\|Z_{i}\|_{2}\times\|Z_{j}\|_{2}}\Big]-p\Big)\Big|{\|Z_{i}\|_{2}=\psi_{i}\;\forall i}\Big]\Big].\\
\end{split} $$

Conditioned on $\{\|Z_{\ell}\|_{2}\}_{\ell=1}^{t},$ the values of $\mathds{1}\Big[\langle V_{i},V_{j}\rangle\geq\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{\|Z_{i}\|_{2}\times\|Z_{j}\|_{2}}\Big]$ are independent since $T$ is a tree by Proposition 3.2. Thus, we can rewrite Eq. 54 as

$$ \begin{split}\E\Big[\prod_{(ji)\in E(T)}\E\Big[\Big(\mathds{1}\Big[\langle V_{i},V_{j}\rangle\geq\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{\|Z_{i}\|_{2}\times\|Z_{j}\|_{2}}\Big]-p\Big)\Big|\{\|Z_{\ell}\|_{2}\}_{\ell=1}^{t},\mathcal{E}\Big]\Big]\end{split} $$

Note that under $\mathcal{E},$ we have that for each $(ji)\in E(T),$ one has

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{\|Z_{i}\|_{2}\times\|Z_{j}\|_{2}}=\rho^{p}_{d}+O\Big(\frac{(\log d)^{3/2}A}{d}\Big). $$

It immediately follows from Corollary 3.6 that for each $(ji)$ one has

$$ \Big|\E\Big[\Big(\mathds{1}\Big[\langle V_{i},V_{j}\rangle\geq\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{\|Z_{i}\|_{2}\times\|Z_{j}\|_{2}}\Big]-p\Big)\;\Big|\;\mathcal{E}\Big]\Big|=O\Big(\frac{p\times(\log d)^{3/2}A}{\sqrt{d}}\Big). $$

The first inequality follows.

Now, by Proposition 3.5 and union bound, with probability $1-|V(T)|\times\exp\Big(-(\log d)^{2}A^{2}\Big)\geq 1-\exp(-(\log d)^{2}|V(T)|/2)=1-o\Big(\Big(p/\sqrt{d}\Big)^{|V(T)|}\Big)$ each $\|Z_{i}\|_{2}$ satisfies $\Big|\|Z_{i}\|_{2}-1\Big|\leq\frac{C\log dA^{2}}{\sqrt{d}}$ for some absolute constant $C.$ Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the event that each $\Big|\|Z_{i}\|_{2}-1\Big|\leq\frac{C\log dA^{2}}{\sqrt{d}}$ holds for all $i.$ Since

$$ \Big|\prod_{(ji)\in E(T)}\E\Big[\Big(\mathds{1}\Big[\langle V_{i},V_{j}\rangle\geq\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{\|Z_{i}\|_{2}\times\|Z_{j}\|_{2}}\Big]-p\Big)\Big|\{\|Z_{\ell}\|_{2}\}_{\ell=1}^{t}\Big]\Big|\leq 1 $$

almost surely, we conclude that

$$ \begin{split}&\Big|\E\Big[\prod_{(ji)\in E(T)}(G_{ji}-p)\Big]\Big|\\
&\leq\Big|\E\Big[\prod_{(ji)\in E(T)}\E\Big[\Big(\mathds{1}\Big[\langle V_{i},V_{j}\rangle\geq\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{\|Z_{i}\|_{2}\times\|Z_{j}\|_{2}}\Big]-p\Big)\Big|\{\|Z_{\ell}\|_{2}\}_{\ell=1}^{t}\Big]\;\Big|\;\mathcal{F}\Big]\Big|+(1-\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[\mathcal{F}])\\
&\leq\Big|\E\Big[\prod_{(ji)\in E(T)}\E\Big[\Big(\mathds{1}\Big[\langle V_{i},V_{j}\rangle\geq\frac{\rho^{p}_{d}}{\|Z_{i}\|_{2}\times\|Z_{j}\|_{2}}\Big]-p\Big)\Big|\{\|Z_{\ell}\|_{2}\}_{\ell=1}^{t}\Big]\;\Big|\;\mathcal{F}\Big]\Big|+o\Big(\Big(\frac{p}{\sqrt{d}}\Big)^{|V(T)|}\Big).\end{split} $$

The second inequality follows. ∎

Now, we can easily combine the statement for trees Lemma A.1 and Theorem 1.1 as follows.

#### Proof of Proposition 3.3.

Let $A=|V(H)|\log d.$ Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the event that each $\Big|\|Z_{i}\|_{2}-1\Big|\leq\frac{|V(H)|\log d}{\sqrt{d}}.$ Clearly, $\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[\mathcal{F}]\geq 1-\exp(-4|V(H)|^{2}\log d)=1-o((p/\sqrt{d})^{|E(H)|}).$ Let also $\mathsf{TP}(H)$ be composed of $k$ trees $T_{1},T_{2},\ldots,T_{H}.$ Then,

### B.1 Proof of Proposition 6.1

#### Proof.

Let $V(H)=[v]$ and let the random labels of vertices are $x_{1},x_{2},\ldots,x_{v}.$

#### 1)

Suppose that, WLOG, $1$ is a leaf and is adjacent to 2. Then,

$$ \displaystyle\E[\mathsf{SW}^{1/2}_{H}(\mathbf{G})]=\E\Big[\E\Big[\prod_{(ji)\in E(H)}(G_{ji}-1/2)\Big|x_{2},x_{3},\ldots,x_{v}\Big]\Big] \displaystyle=\E\Big[\prod_{(ji)\in E(H)\backslash\{(21)\}}(G_{ji}-1/2)\E\Big[(G_{21}-1/2)\Big|x_{2},x_{3},\ldots,x_{v}\Big]\Big]. $$

The last expectation equals zero. Indeed,

$$ \E\Big[(G_{21}-1/2)\Big|x_{2},x_{3},\ldots,x_{v}\Big]=\frac{1}{2}\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[x_{1}=x_{2}]-\frac{1}{2(q-1)}\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[x_{1}\neq x_{2}]=\frac{1}{2q}-\frac{1}{2(q-1)}\times\frac{q-1}{q}=0. $$

#### 2)

We compute $\E[(G_{21}-1/2)(G_{31}-1/2)(G_{32}-1/2)]$ based on the number of equalities among labels.

- 1. All three labels are equal with probability $\frac{1}{q^{2}}.$ In that case,

$$ \E[(G_{21}-1/2)(G_{31}-1/2)(G_{32}-1/2)|x_{1}=x_{2}=x_{3}]=\frac{1}{8}. $$

- 2. Two of the labels are equal and the third is different with probability $\frac{3(q-1)}{q^{2}}.$ In that case,

$$ \E[(G_{21}-1/2)(G_{31}-1/2)(G_{32}-1/2)|x_{1}=x_{2}\neq x_{3}]=\frac{1}{8(q-1)^{2}}. $$

- 3. All three labels are distinct with probability $\frac{(q-1)(q-2)}{q^{2}}.$ In that case,

$$ \E[(G_{21}-1/2)(G_{31}-1/2)(G_{32}-1/2)|x_{1}\neq x_{2}\neq x_{3}]=-\frac{1}{8(q-1)^{3}}. $$

#### 3)

Clearly, it is enough to prove the claim for $H$ connected. Suppose that the labels partition $V(H)$ into sets $C_{1},C_{2},\ldots,C_{m},$ determined by label equalities, i.e. $a,b$ are in the same $C_{i}$ if and only if $x_{a}=x_{b}.$ Clearly, there are at most $|V(H)|^{|V(H)|-1}$ such partitions.

Furthermore, each partition $C_{1},C_{2},\ldots,C_{m}$ occurs with probability at most $\prod_{i=1}^{m}(1/q)^{|C_{i}|-1}=(1/q)^{|V(H)|-m}$ as in each $C_{i},$ the probability that all vertices get the same label as the lexicographically first one is $(1/q)^{|C_{i}|-1}.$ Finally, suppose that there are $k$ edges with two endpoints in different sets $C_{i},C_{j}.$ Then,

$$ \E\Big[\prod_{(ji)\in E(H)}(G_{ji}-1/2)|C_{1},C_{2},\ldots,C_{m}\Big]=\Big(\frac{1}{2}\Big)^{|E(H)|-k}\times\Big(-\frac{1}{2(q-1)}\Big)^{k}. $$

However, as $H$ is connected, $k\geq m-1.$ Hence, the above expression is at most $(1/q)^{m-1}$ in absolute value. Summing over the $|V(H)|^{|V(H)|-1}$ partitions gives the result. ∎

### B.2 The Low-Degree $\chi^{2}$ calculation

Finally, note that we defined $\widehat{w}_{H}\coloneqq M_{H,H}w_{H}.$ However, $M_{H,H}\geq 1-|V(H)|^{2}/q\geq 1/2$ whenever $q=\tilde{\Theta}(d^{-1/4}),|V(H)|\leq(\log n)^{1.1}=\mathsf{polylog}(d)$ under (A). $$ \begin{split}&\sum_{H\;:\;1\leq|E(H)|\leq D}w_{H}^{2}\\

Observe that whenever $q\geq n^{2/3+c},$ equivalently $d\geq n^{8/3+c}$ by Eq. 28, the last expression is of the form

$$ \sum_{v=1}^{2D}\sum_{e=1}^{\max(D,\binom{v}{2})}v^{2e}n^{-\theta v} $$

for some positive constant $v.$ However, $e\log v\leq v\times(e/v\log v)\leq v\sqrt{e}\log v\leq v\sqrt{D}\log v\leq v(\log n)^{.6}=o(v\log n).$ Thus, the sum is bounded by

$$ \sum_{v=1}^{2D}\sum_{e=1}^{\max(D,\binom{v}{2})}n^{-\theta v/2}=o_{n}(1), $$

&=\sum_{H\subseteq E(K_{n})\;:\;0\leq|E(H)|\leq D}\widehat{f}(H)\sqrt{\psi_{q}(1-\psi_{q})}^{-|E(H)|}\times\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\times\Big(\sum_{K\subseteq H}\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[\mathbf{X}|_{E(H)}=E(H)\backslash E(K)](1-\psi_{q})^{E(H)\backslash E(K)}\prod_{(ji)\in E(K)}(\mathbf{H}_{ji}-\psi_{q})\Big)\\
&=\sum_{K\subseteq E(K_{n})\;:\;0\leq|E(K)|\leq D}\Big(\sqrt{\psi_{q}(1-\psi_{q})}^{-|E(K)|}\prod_{(ji)\in E(K)}(\mathbf{H}_{ji}-\psi_{q})\times\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\sum_{H\subseteq K_{n}\;:\;0\leq|E(H)|\leq D,E(K)\subseteq E(H)}\widehat{f}(H)\,{\rm I}\kern-1.79993pt{\rm P}[\mathbf{X}|_{E(H)}=E(H)\backslash E(K)]\sqrt{(1-\psi_{q})/\psi_{q}}^{E(H)\backslash E(K)}\Big)\\
&=\sum_{K\subseteq E(K_{n})\;:\;0\leq|E(K)|\leq D}\sqrt{\psi_{q}(1-\psi_{q})}^{-|E(K)|}\prod_{(ji)\in E(K)}(\mathbf{H}_{ji}-\psi_{q})\times\sum_{H\subseteq K_{n}\;:\;0\leq|E(H)|\leq D,E(K)\subseteq E(H)}M_{K,H}\widehat{f}(H),\end{split} $$

where $M$ is the upper-triangular matrix indexed by subgraphs of cardinality at most $D$ and defined by the above equation.

Now, since $\mathbf{H}\sim\mathsf{G}(n,\psi_{q}),$ the polynomials

$$ \Big\{\sqrt{\psi_{q}(1-\psi_{q})}^{-|E(K)|}\prod_{(ji)\in E(K)}(\mathbf{H}_{ji}-\psi_{q})\Big\}_{K\subseteq E(K_{n})\;:\;1\leq|E(K)|\leq D} $$

are orthonormal with respect to the measure of $\mathbf{H}$ (see Eq. 16). Hence,

$$ \displaystyle\E_{\mathbf{H}\sim\mathsf{G}(n,\psi_{q})}\Big[g(\mathbf{H})^{2}\Big] \displaystyle=\sum_{K\subseteq E(K_{n})\;:\;0\leq|E(K)|\leq D}\Big(\sum_{H\subseteq K_{n}\;:\;0\leq|E(H)|\leq D,E(K)\subseteq E(H)}M_{K,H}\widehat{f}(H)\Big)^{2} \displaystyle=\|M\widehat{f}_{\leq D}\|^{2}_{2}. $$

Thus,

$$ \displaystyle\begin{split}&\frac{\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}}[f(\mathbf{G})]}{\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathsf{PCol}(n,q)}[f(\mathbf{G})^{2}]^{1/2}}=\frac{\langle\widehat{f}_{\leq D},(\Phi^{\psi_{q}}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})})(\leq D)\rangle}{\|M\widehat{f}_{\leq D}\|_{2}}.\end{split} $$

A simple Cauchy-Schwartz argument as in [KVWX23] shows that the above expression is at most $\|w\|_{2},$ where $w\coloneqq(M^{-1})^{T}(\Phi^{\psi_{q}}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})})(\leq D).$ Using the upper-triangular structure of $M,$ one can find

$$ w_{H}\coloneqq\frac{1}{M_{H,H}}\Big(\Phi^{\psi_{q}}_{\mathsf{RGG}(n,\mathbb{S}^{d-1},\frac{1}{2})}(H)-\sum_{K\subsetneq H}w_{K}M_{K,H}\Big), $$

as long as $M_{H,H}\geq 0$ holds for all $H.$ ∎
